job.title: 2027 Finance Graduate Program (Darwin)
job.description:
Take your career somewhere unexpected

The Northern Territory Department of Treasury and Finance is looking for 10+ graduates to join our 2027 Graduate Program in Darwin.

Over 12 months, you'll complete three rotations across Treasury, work on real projects and learn alongside experienced professionals and senior leaders.

You’ll build meaningful experience early, take on real responsibility and discover where your strengths could take you.

What you'll get

  • Starting salary of $76,155 + super
  • Six weeks' annual recreation leave
  • Three weeks' personal leave
  • An additional three days' Christmas shutdown leave
  • Three rotations across Treasury
  • Structured learning and professional development
  • Exposure to experienced professionals and senior leaders
  • Opportunities to continue building your career within Treasury or the wider NT Government


Relocating to Darwin? We'll help make the move easier.
Graduate relocation support includes:

  • A one-way economy flight to Darwin
  • Up to 14 days' temporary accommodation
  • Up to $4,000 in removal assistance
  • Eligible vehicle and pet relocation costs can also be covered within the removal allowance.


Who we're looking for
We're particularly interested in graduates from:

  • Economics and Finance
  • Accounting, Business and Commerce
  • Data, Analytics, Mathematics and Statistics
  • Law and related disciplines

You can apply if you've completed an eligible degree at a recognised Australian university or institute within the past three years, or you're due to graduate before the program commences.

You'll also need to be either:

  • An Australian citizen
  • An Australian permanent resident, or
  • A visa holder with appropriate working rights


Go further, faster
This isn't a graduate program where you'll spend 12 months watching from the sidelines.

Depending on your rotations, you could contribute to the Territory Budget, economic modelling, financial reporting, revenue forecasting, policy development, legislation, major Territory investments and advice that informs government decision-making. Rotations may include:

  • Financial Management
  • Economics
  • Territory Revenue

You can take on significant responsibility early, with the support and supervision to learn as you go.


Where could your career be in 5 years? Plot twist: you live in the Territory.
Yes, the job is in Darwin.

A move to the Northern Territory isn't just a career decision. It's a lifestyle change.

Less time sitting in traffic. More time outside. Warm weather, incredible landscapes, a close-knit community and some of Australia's most extraordinary places within reach. You could finish work with enough time left in the day to actually do something with it.

Your commute just got shorter. Your weekends got bigger.
Spend your weekends exploring national parks and swimming holes. Head to the markets. Get out on the water. Find your new local. Or jump on a flight and explore more of Australia and Asia.

And with six weeks of annual recreation leave, you'll have more time to make the most of it. You don't have to choose between building your career and having a life outside it.


Go further at work. Live bigger outside it. Ready to see where it could take you?
You don't need to have your entire career mapped out.

If you're curious, ambitious and ready to put your degree to work on something meaningful, we'd like to hear from you.


Location: Darwin, Northern Territory
Program: 12 months, full-time
Commencement: 15 January 2027
Applications close: 30 September 2026

Ready to go further? Apply now.
Please apply with current resume and cover letter in Microsoft Word format only (.doc or .docx).

For enquiries, please email NTGrad@davidsonwp.com

Want to know more about Davidson? Visit us at www.davidsonwp.com

job.title: Senior Communications Advisor – Major Infrastructure
job.description:
About the Company
Davidson is partnering with a Queensland Government organisation delivering a significant pipeline of major transport infrastructure projects across the Sunshine Coast.

With several transformational projects moving through active delivery, an opportunity is available for an experienced Senior Communications Advisor to join a regional Communications and Stakeholder Engagement team.

This is an exceptional long-term opportunity for someone who enjoys being close to project delivery and working collaboratively with project teams, contractors, technical specialists and the community.

About the Role
This is not a traditional corporate communications role.

You will be embedded within major infrastructure project delivery, leading communications and stakeholder engagement activities across designated project packages and working closely with both government and contractor delivery teams.

Your role will be highly varied and hands-on. One day you may be developing the stakeholder approach for an upcoming traffic change, while the next could involve responding to community concerns, advising a project manager on an emerging issue or coordinating communications around a significant construction milestone.

Key responsibilities will include:

  • Lead communications and stakeholder engagement planning across major infrastructure project packages.
  • Work closely with project managers, principal contractors and delivery partners to coordinate timely and accurate communications.
  • Plan and deliver communications relating to construction works, traffic changes, project milestones and community impacts.
  • Build productive relationships with councils, government agencies, businesses, community groups and affected stakeholders.
  • Develop and quality assure project notifications, community updates, consultation materials, stakeholder briefings and other communications.
  • Provide strategic advice on stakeholder engagement, emerging issues and reputational risks.
  • Proactively identify and help mitigate community and stakeholder risks associated with project delivery.
  • Translate complex engineering, technical and construction information into clear and accessible public messaging.
  • Manage sensitive stakeholder matters, enquiries and competing priorities with sound judgement.
  • Monitor community sentiment and stakeholder feedback to help inform project decision-making.
  • Represent the project at stakeholder, contractor and community meetings as required.

About You
You will be an experienced communications and stakeholder engagement professional who is confident operating in complex project and construction environments.

We are particularly interested in hearing from candidates with experience across transport infrastructure, civil construction, major projects, alliances, joint ventures or contractor-delivered projects.

To be successful, you will ideally bring:

  • Demonstrated experience delivering communications and stakeholder engagement for major infrastructure or construction projects.
  • Strong exposure to active construction and project delivery, including communicating construction impacts, traffic changes or disruptions.
  • Experience working alongside principal contractors, alliance partners, engineering teams or multidisciplinary project teams.
  • Strong stakeholder relationship management skills and the confidence to influence and advise at senior levels.
  • Experience managing community concerns, complaints, sensitive issues and stakeholder risks.
  • Excellent written communication skills, including the ability to turn complex technical information into clear public messaging.
  • Experience developing communications and engagement strategies, project updates, notifications, briefings and consultation materials.
  • The ability to operate independently, exercise sound judgement and manage competing priorities in a fast-moving environment.
  • A proactive and solutions-focused approach to stakeholder and community engagement.

Previous Queensland Government or transport infrastructure experience will be highly regarded but is not essential.

IAP2 certification or tertiary qualifications in Communications, Public Relations, Journalism, Marketing, Stakeholder Engagement or a related discipline will also be viewed favourably.

The Benefits

  • Long-term 5 year contract through
  • $79.18 – $84.55 per hour + superannuation, dependent on experience and approved classification.
  • Work on significant, high-profile transport infrastructure projects on the Sunshine Coast.
  • Opportunity to work directly alongside government, contractors and multidisciplinary project delivery teams.
  • A genuinely hands-on role where your work will directly influence the stakeholder and community experience of major project delivery.
  • Buderim / Sunshine Coast location.


Please apply with your current resume in Microsoft Word format only (.doc or .docx.) For further information about Davidson and the opportunities we recruit across Australia, visit www.davidsonwp.com.

job.title: AO3 Project Support Officer - Sunshine Coast
job.description:
About the Company

Davidson is partnering with a Queensland Government organisation responsible for delivering significant transport infrastructure projects across the Sunshine Coast.

This is an excellent opportunity to contribute to two major projects while building your experience within a high-profile government infrastructure environment.

About the Role

As the AO3 Project Support Officer, you will provide day-to-day administrative, coordination and project support to Project Managers and broader project teams.

Working closely with internal stakeholders, you will help maintain effective project governance by ensuring documentation, reporting and administrative processes are accurate, organised and completed on time.

  • Managing project documentation, filing, version control and document registers.
  • Coordinating document submissions, approvals, revisions and associated workflows.
  • Maintaining electronic document management systems, including SharePoint, InEight, DMS or similar platforms.
  • Establishing and maintaining project registers, correspondence logs and administrative systems.
  • Coordinating meetings and preparing agendas, supporting documentation and minutes.
  • Providing administrative support to Project Managers and broader project teams.
  • Maintaining spreadsheets and assisting with basic project reporting.
  • Liaising with internal stakeholders to obtain and clarify project information.
  • Preparing project correspondence using Microsoft Office applications.
  • Supporting records management, data entry, filing and general project administration.
  • Ensuring documentation and administrative processes comply with quality and records management requirements.

About You

You will be an organised and detail-focused administration professional who can confidently manage competing priorities within a busy project environment.

  • Previous experience in project administration, project support or a similar administrative position.
  • Strong document control and records management experience.
  • Experience using SharePoint, electronic document management systems or comparable platforms.
  • Strong Microsoft Office skills, particularly Word and Excel.
  • Excellent organisational skills and attention to detail.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Confidence engaging with stakeholders at varying levels.
  • The ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.

Experience within Queensland Government, transport or major infrastructure projects will be highly regarded.

A current Class C driver’s licence is desirable.

The Benefits

  • Competitive rate of $51.13 - $56.72 per hour + super per hour plus superannuation.
  • Initial 2 year contract with potential for extesion
  • AO3 opportunity within a Queensland Government organisation.
  • Contribute to two significant transport infrastructure projects.
  • Gain valuable exposure to project delivery, governance and document control.
  • Convenient Maroochydore, Sunshine Coast location.
  • Work across varied project administration and stakeholder coordination activities.
  • The successful candidate will be required to complete a criminal history check before appointment.


Please submit your current resume to apply, quoting reference JN -092026-44194. To learn more about Davidson, visit davidsonwp.com.

job.title: Chief Executive Officer - Alliance Française de Melbourne
job.description:
• Shape strategy, culture and commercial performance in a high-profile, purpose-led organisation
  • Grow revenue, audiences and partnerships while expanding French language and cultural engagement
  • Lead a talented team and work closely with the Board to build a sustainable, contemporary organisation

Lead the next chapter of Melbourne’s premier French language and cultural organisation, shaping growth, impact and long-term sustainability.

About the Organisation

Founded in 1890, the Alliance Française de Melbourne is an independent, not-for-profit organisation and Victoria’s leading centre for French language and culture. Through language education, examinations, cultural programs, partnerships and community events, it creates meaningful connections between the people of Victoria and the diverse cultures of the French-speaking world.

Now operating from its new French Hub in the heart of Melbourne, Alliance Française de Melbourne is entering an important new chapter. With a proud history, an internationally recognised brand and an engaged community of students, members, educators, partners and supporters, the organisation is focused on strengthening its sustainability, broadening its reach and building a contemporary organisation for the future.

About the Role:

Reporting to the Chair of the Board, the Chief Executive Officer will provide the strategic, commercial and operational leadership required to deliver Alliance Française de Melbourne’s next phase of development. Leading a multidisciplinary team, you will translate the organisation’s strategy into clear priorities, strengthen organisational capability and ensure that its educational and cultural mission is supported by a sustainable and well-managed business.

You will also provide executive leadership to the newly established Alliance Française de Melbourne Cultural Foundation, helping build its philanthropic, cultural and revenue-generating potential.

Key priorities will include:

  • Leading the implementation of the organisation’s strategy and establishing clear measures of performance, accountability and impact.
  • Strengthening financial sustainability by growing and diversifying revenue across education, cultural programs, partnerships, memberships, philanthropy and venue opportunities.
  • Building a capable, connected and high-performing team, supported by contemporary systems, clear responsibilities and a positive organisational culture.
  • Growing Alliance Française de Melbourne’s profile, audiences and community engagement while ensuring its programs remain relevant, accessible and distinctive.
  • Developing productive relationships with the Board, employees, educators, members, government, the French diplomatic and cultural network, commercial partners and the wider Victorian community.
  • Leading the development of the newly established Cultural Foundation, working with its Board to grow philanthropy, sponsorship and revenue-generating cultural opportunities.

This is an opportunity to respect and build upon a significant legacy while bringing the commercial discipline, organisational clarity and fresh thinking needed to secure its future.

The role requires flexibility to support Alliance Française de Melbourne’s cultural and community activities, including availability outside standard business hours when required.

The role will commence in early January 2027.

About You:

You will be an adaptable and values-led leader who can operate confidently across strategy, commercial performance, people leadership and stakeholder engagement. You will bring:

  • Senior leadership experience from within a purpose-led, educational, cultural, membership, community or similarly multifaceted organisation.
  • Strong commercial and financial capability, including experience improving performance, developing new revenue streams and managing resources responsibly.
  • Demonstrated success leading organisational change, strengthening teams and converting strategy into practical and measurable outcomes.
  • Highly developed communication, influencing and relationship-building skills, with the confidence to work effectively with a governing Board and a diverse stakeholder community.
  • Fluent in French language and a genuine interest in French culture, together with the cultural intelligence to connect an Australian organisation with an established international network.

You will combine an entrepreneurial mindset with sound judgement and operational discipline. Equally comfortable engaging with community members, educators, partners and directors, you will understand how to balance mission, heritage and commercial sustainability. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and experiences.

To view the Success Profile for this opportunity, please copy and paste the following link into your browser: https://tinyurl.com/2bm3nf7a

To apply, please click ‘apply now’ and upload your CV and Cover Letter. For any questions not outlined in the success profile and for a confidential discussion, please contact Alex Mummé at 0474 434 868 / Alex.Mumme@davidsonwp.com or Danielle Walker at 0402 278 870 / Danielle.Walker@davidsonwp.com

job.title: Relocation Opportunity | HR Advisor
job.description:
HR Advisor | Workforce & People

Katherine West Health Board | Katherine, NT

$94,907 – $116,569 + 12% super | Salary packaging | Relocation support


Make your next HR role mean something.


Are you an experienced HR Advisor looking for broader exposure, greater autonomy and the opportunity to work somewhere your contribution genuinely matters?

Davidson is proud to partner with Katherine West Health Board (KWHB), an Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Organisation providing primary healthcare and health-related programs to Aboriginal communities across approximately 162,000km² of the remote Katherine West region.

KWHB has experienced significant organisational growth and is continuing to strengthen its Human Resources function to support its expanding workforce.

We're now seeking an experienced HR Advisor to join the team in Katherine.

Internally titled Workforce Coordinator, this is a broad, hands-on HR advisory role working closely with the Senior Manager Human Resources and supporting managers and employees across the organisation.

If you enjoy variety, like being close to the action and want the opportunity to develop across the breadth of HR rather than being confined to one specialist area, this could be a fantastic next move.


The opportunity

You'll become a trusted member of a growing HR team, providing practical advice and support across the employee lifecycle.

No two days are likely to look exactly the same.

You'll support managers with day-to-day HR matters, prepare employment documentation, oversee workforce compliance, contribute to HR reporting and process improvement, and help ensure employees joining KWHB have a consistent and culturally appropriate experience.

You'll also have exposure to workplace reviews and investigations, workforce planning and broader organisational improvement initiatives.


Your responsibilities will include:

  • Providing practical HR advice and support to managers and employees
  • Interpreting and applying HR policies, procedures, employment legislation and relevant industrial instruments
  • Preparing contracts, variations, secondments and other employment documentation
  • Supporting recruitment, onboarding, induction and offboarding
  • Monitoring licences, registrations, checks, certifications and other workforce compliance requirements
  • Supporting remuneration changes, pay progression, allowances and contractual changes
  • Maintaining accurate employee records and HR information systems
  • Coordinating workforce logistics including travel, accommodation and remote workforce requirements
  • Preparing workforce reporting and identifying trends, risks and opportunities
  • Contributing to HR policy, procedure and process improvement
  • Supporting workplace reviews and investigations as required
  • Contributing to culturally appropriate induction, orientation and workforce development activities.


    The position also provides an opportunity to support and mentor less experienced HR and administrative team members as the function continues to evolve.


    About you
    We're looking for an experienced HR generalist who is comfortable providing practical advice and doesn't need every answer handed to them.

    You don't need to be the finished product or an ER/IR specialist. You do, however, need enough HR experience and judgement to work through an issue, interpret the relevant policy or legislation, provide sensible advice and recognise when something needs to be escalated.

    You'll ideally bring:
  • Experience at HR Advisor, People & Culture Advisor, Senior HR Coordinator or similar level
  • Practical experience providing HR advice and support to managers
  • Sound knowledge of HR policies, procedures and relevant employment legislation
  • Experience across employment documentation and employee lifecycle processes
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Confidence managing multiple priorities and working autonomously
  • Strong administration, systems and attention to detail
  • Sound judgement, discretion and professionalism
  • A practical, solutions-focused approach
  • The ability to build trusted relationships across a diverse and geographically dispersed workforce.


    Experience in health, community services, government, not-for-profit or an Aboriginal Community Controlled Organisation would be highly regarded, but isn't essential.

    A qualification in Human Resources, Business or a related discipline is desirable rather than mandatory, with equivalent relevant experience also considered.

    Working with Katherine West Health Board

    This role is about more than providing HR advice from behind a desk.

    KWHB supports employees across Katherine and remote Aboriginal communities throughout the Katherine West region. You'll work with people from diverse professional, cultural and community backgrounds and will need to approach those relationships with respect, curiosity and cultural humility.

    KWHB is committed to the recruitment, retention and development of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander employees and to creating culturally safe workplaces where people can develop meaningful careers.

    You'll occasionally travel to remote communities by road and/or light aircraft as part of the role.

    What's on offer?
  • $94,907 – $116,569 + 12% super, negotiable based on relevant skills and experience
  • 6 weeks annual leave + 18% leave loading
  • 2 weeks personal leave
  • Annual CPI increases
  • Salary packaging up to $15,900 per FBT year
  • Meal & Entertainment Card up to $2,650
  • Remote Area Benefits
  • Novated leasing
  • Relocation assistance up to $3,000
  • 6–8 weeks accommodation support on relocation
  • Travel allowance for work-related travel
  • Mobile phone allowance
  • Flexible working arrangements
  • Generous professional development support
  • Strong internal career pathways
  • The opportunity to build a career within a respected Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Organisation.


    Before you apply

    This is a full-time permanent role based in Katherine, Northern Territory.

    The successful candidate will need:
  • A current NT Driver's Licence or the ability to obtain one
  • A current NT Working with Children Clearance (Ochre Card) or ability to obtain
  • A current Criminal History Check or ability to obtain
  • COVID-19 immunisation – minimum one dose
  • High-level computer skills including Microsoft Office and HR information systems
  • The ability and willingness to travel to remote locations by road and/or light aircraft
  • A demonstrated understanding of Aboriginal cultural values and commitment to the advancement and self-determination of Aboriginal communities.

    KWHB is also open to considering suitably experienced candidates already living in Australia on a visa, subject to assessment of individual visa conditions and work rights.

    Candidates across Australia and New Zealand who are genuinely prepared to relocate to Katherine are encouraged to apply.

    Interested?

    If you're an HR Advisor looking for an opportunity that offers breadth, autonomy, purpose and the chance to make a meaningful contribution within a growing organisation, we'd love to hear from you.

    To apply - Please note:

    Due to the quick turnaround for this opportunity and anticipated application volumes, please submit your application directly through the advertised application link rather than emailing your resume to the consultant - This will ensure your application is captured promptly as part of the recruitment process.

    Please apply with current resume in Microsoft Word format only (.doc or .docx) through the application portal. If you would like to have a confidential discussion, please contact Taylah Gurney. Want to know more about Davidson? Visit us at www.davidsonwp.com

job.title: Executive Assistant to CEO & CFO
job.description:
About the Company
Davidson is partnering with a well established Australian organisation with a significant national footprint and diverse business operations.

Operating within a fast paced and commercially focused environment, the organisation has an established presence within its sector and continues to grow and evolve. This newly created position will work closely with two key members of the Executive Leadership Team and will play an important role in establishing a highly effective executive support function.


About the Role
We are seeking an experienced Executive Assistant to provide high level support to the CEO and CFO.

As a newly created position, this is an opportunity to genuinely shape the role. You will establish effective ways of working, introduce structure and processes and develop an executive support function that enables both leaders to operate effectively.

This role extends well beyond traditional diary management. You will become a trusted point of connection between the CEO, CFO, senior leaders and key external stakeholders, with exposure across executive communications, meetings, travel, projects, reporting and broader strategic, financial and operational priorities.

Key responsibilities will include:

  • Establishing and developing the executive support function for the CEO and CFO
  • Proactively managing complex diaries, meetings, commitments and competing priorities
  • Developing effective systems for actions, follow ups, correspondence and executive priorities
  • Coordinating domestic and international travel, including detailed itineraries and briefing materials
  • Preparing executive correspondence, presentations, reports, agendas and business papers
  • Anticipating requirements and addressing matters before they become issues
  • Acting as a highly professional point of contact for senior internal and external stakeholders
  • Managing sensitive and commercially confidential information with discretion
  • Supporting executive meetings, leadership forums, events and key business engagements
  • Providing coordination support across strategic, operational and finance related projects
  • Travelling with the CEO on occasion to support external meetings, events and business engagements


    About You
    You will be an accomplished Executive Assistant who has previously supported a CEO, CFO, Managing Director or similarly senior executive.

    Importantly, you will have experience stepping into an environment where you have needed to create structure, establish processes and build an executive support role around the needs of your executive, rather than simply maintaining established systems.

    You will be proactive, commercially aware and confident using your judgement. You understand how to represent senior executives professionally and can communicate credibly with stakeholders at all levels.

    We are looking for:
  • Significant experience supporting C suite or equivalent senior executives
  • Experience establishing or significantly developing an Executive Assistant function or newly created role
  • Proven ability to manage complex and frequently changing executive priorities
  • Strong judgement with the confidence to make decisions and operate independently
  • Exceptional organisation, attention to detail and follow through
  • Highly developed written and verbal communication skills
  • A polished and professional approach when representing senior executives and the organisation
  • Strong stakeholder management skills with experience engaging senior internal and external stakeholders
  • Strong commercial awareness and the ability to understand broader business priorities
  • Flexibility and willingness to travel when required
  • The ability to confidently converse in Mandarin when engaging with Mandarin speaking stakeholders. Full professional fluency, reading and writing capability are not required


    The Benefits
  • Newly created role with the opportunity to genuinely shape the executive support function
  • Direct exposure to the CEO, CFO and broader Executive Leadership Team
  • High level of autonomy and ownership within a trusted senior position
  • Broad exposure across strategic, commercial, financial and operational priorities
  • Opportunity to work within an established Australian organisation with a significant national footprint
  • Varied role combining executive support, stakeholder engagement, projects, travel and business coordination



    To learn more about Davidson, visit davidsonwp.com.

job.title: Kraken M2C Solution Architect
job.description:
JOB OVERVIEW

JOB TITLE: Kraken M2C Solution Architect
JOB LOCATION: Melbourne, VIC (Hybrid)
JOB DURATION: 12 months

We are seeking an experienced Solution Architect with strong utilities and Meter-to-Cash expertise, including hands-on experience with Kraken implementations or conversions, to support a major transformation program.

This is an exciting opportunity to work on large-scale utility transformation initiatives, designing scalable end-to-end solutions across smart metering, customer, billing and meter data platforms.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Design end-to-end Meter-to-Cash solution architectures across the utilities landscape.
  • Define integration strategies across CIS, MDM, CRM and billing platforms.
  • Lead architecture workshops and solution design sessions with clients and stakeholders.
  • Design scalable solutions capable of processing high-volume smart meter data.
  • Develop architecture blueprints, solution designs and technology roadmaps.
  • Provide architecture governance throughout project delivery.
  • Work closely with product, technology and business teams to ensure solution alignment.
  • Drive the adoption of AI and automation aligned with the product and transformation strategy.
  • Identify and manage technical risks, dependencies and cross-system considerations.
  • Act as a trusted technical advisor to utility clients throughout major transformation programs.

Key Skills & Experience:

  • Strong domain expertise across utilities, Meter-to-Cash, smart metering and Meter Data Management (MDM).
  • Proven experience with Kraken, particularly implementation, conversion or migration programs.
  • Strong understanding of utility platforms, systems, integrations and end-to-end business processes.
  • Experience working within Agile environments with iterative development, configuration and deployment cycles.
  • Strong systems-thinking capability, with the ability to navigate complex cross-system dependencies.
  • Hands-on delivery experience across large-scale, multi-year software migrations or transformation programs, particularly within utility distributors.
  • Strong understanding of global utility markets, smart metering networks and complex billing/regulatory environments.
  • Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to lead architecture discussions and influence senior stakeholders.



Please submit your current resume to apply. If you'd like a confidential discussion about the role, please contact Bidisha Swayamprava on Bidisha.Swayamprava@davidsonwp.com, quoting reference JN -092026-44188. To learn more about Davidson, visit davidsonwp.com.

job.title: Project Delivery and Control Officer
job.description:
About the Company

Davidson Technology are working with a State Government Department to secure a Project Delivery and Control Officer to provide project coordination, reporting, project controls, and administrative support services across Operational Data Systems.


About the Role

As the Project Delivery will provide high-quality project coordination, reporting, project controls and administrative support within department’s Operational Data Systems (ODS) team, supporting a diverse portfolio of technology and operational initiatives including the Operational Data Centre (ODC), Traffic Count Program (TCP), Critical Safety Middleware (CSM) and Cyber Security. You will coordinate project meetings, workshops and delivery activities, prepare agendas and executive reporting materials, accurately capture minutes, actions, decisions, risks and issues, and proactively follow up stakeholders to ensure actions progress to closure. You will maintain professional and accurate project documentation and repositories in Confluence, support project tracking, reporting and change activities through Jira, and develop and continuously improve templates, reporting standards, registers and documentation processes. You will monitor actions, risks, issues, decisions and change requests across multiple concurrent initiatives, ensuring stakeholders receive accurate and timely information while providing the structured project controls and administrative support required to keep delivery activities organised and on track.


About You

To be successful in this role, you’ll bring demonstrated experience in project delivery, project controls, coordination or administration, with strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities, recurring deliverables and competing deadlines while maintaining a high level of accuracy and attention to detail. You will have excellent written communication skills, with experience preparing professional reports, executive reporting packs, meeting minutes and project documentation, and the ability to translate discussions and decisions into clear actions and proactively follow these through to completion. job.title: Board Chair - Carers Victoria
job.description:
• Strengthen Carers Victoria’s voice, influence and impact for carers
  • Lead a highly capable Board with contemporary governance
  • Partner with an experienced CEO and influence key stakeholders

Carers Victoria is the statewide peak body for unpaid carers and a leading provider of support, advice and connection for people in care relationships. Established in 1992, the organisation has a proud history of advocating for carers and working to enhance the health and wellbeing of carers and the people they support. As an ACNC-registered charity, Carers Victoria plays a dual role: delivering practical assistance to carers while influencing government policy, raising awareness and ensuring the voices and experiences of carers inform decision-making. With strong financial foundations, an experienced leadership team and a highly capable Board, Carers Victoria is focused on strengthening its organisational capability, expanding its reach and continuing to increase its impact for carers.

Carers Victoria is seeking an accomplished and experienced Board Chair to lead its skills-based Board through its next chapter. Working in close partnership with the Chief Executive Officer and fellow Directors, the Chair will provide contemporary governance leadership, maintain a clear focus on strategy and ensure the Board operates effectively and efficiently within a highly regulated and government-funded environment. The Chair will foster constructive debate, draw on the diverse expertise around the Board table and ensure appropriate separation between governance and operations. They will also play an important ambassadorial role, working alongside the CEO to strengthen relationships and influence across Victorian and Federal Government, the community sector and other key stakeholders.

You will be an experienced Board Chair with substantial governance experience and a demonstrated ability to lead a capable Board through complexity. Personable, authentic and contemporary in your approach, you will know how to facilitate effective decision-making, manage different perspectives and build a strong and appropriately challenging partnership with an experienced CEO. You will ideally bring experience within a highly regulated, government-funded or care-related environment, with an understanding of care governance and strong government and stakeholder networks highly regarded. Experience navigating organisational transformation or significant change will also be valuable. A genuine understanding of carers and caring relationships is important, with personal lived experience of caring highly regarded. Above all, you will bring sound judgement, strong interpersonal capability and a commitment to ensuring the voices of carers remain central to Carers Victoria's future.

job.title: Associate Utilities Commissioners
job.description:
• Shape the future of essential utility regulation in the NT
  • Bring practical judgement to complex regulatory issues
  • Make a high-impact contribution in a flexible, part-time role

The Utilities Commission of the Northern Territory is a statutory authority established under the Utilities Commission Act 2000 and is the independent economic regulator for the Northern Territory. The Commission is constituted by the Utilities Commissioner and Associate Commissioners and has responsibility across regulated industries, including electricity, ports, water and sewerage.

The object of the Utilities Commission Act 2000 is to establish an economic regulatory framework that promotes and safeguards competition and fair and efficient market conduct. The Commission’s primary purpose is to protect the long-term interests of Territory consumers of services provided by regulated industries, particularly in relation to price, reliability and quality. Its vision is to benefit Territorians through effective regulation, well-informed and transparent decision-making and robust, independent advice.

Planned succession has created two Associate Utilities Commissioner opportunities for experienced professionals to contribute to the Commission’s next chapter and to the effective regulation of essential services for Territorians. Working with the Commissioner, the Associate Utilities Commissioners will contribute to regulatory decisions, strategic direction and oversight of the Commission’s work.

These are flexible, part-time appointments of approximately one day per week. The role is to:

  • support the Utilities Commissioner to deliver the Commission’s statutory functions, and set and achieve the Commission’s strategy and priorities
  • contribute expertise to, and be part of, the Commission’s collective decision-making and advice provision
  • engage with Ministers, government officials, regulated entities, consumers, industry and other regulators, including through meetings and site visits
  • support, and contribute to the development of, Commission staff
  • uphold, and foster a positive culture consistent with, the Commission’s values.

This is an active and hands-on role. The Associate Utilities Commissioners will be expected to understand complex issues, identify key considerations, provide guidance to staff and contribute constructively to regulatory approaches and decisions. The role also involves direct engagement with CEOs, boards, Ministers and other senior stakeholders.

While the role is part-time, it requires flexibility to review detailed material and respond to matters within agreed timeframes outside regular meetings and requires periodic travel to the Northern Territory. Travel is expected to be approximately once per quarter, primarily to Darwin, with the possibility of one annual visit to a regional area outside Darwin.

To be considered for this role, you will bring substantial experience in economic regulation, water or energy regulation, regulated utilities, government policy, law, economics, consulting or a related field. Your experience will be practical and applied, with the judgement to translate complex regulatory, commercial and policy issues into clear advice and decisions.

Your experience may have been gained as a regulator, economist, lawyer, senior executive, consultant, board member or leader within a regulated business. You will be comfortable operating at Commissioner level while engaging sufficiently in detail to support a small specialist team.

You will bring independence, sound judgement and the confidence to express clear views, together with a collaborative approach to working with fellow Commissioners, staff and stakeholders. A high level of integrity, objectivity and professionalism is fundamental.

Candidates must be available for periodic travel to the Northern Territory and able to accommodate a flexible part-time commitment. The appointments are expected to commence in late 2026 or early 2027, subject to relevant approval processes.

  • Provide accurate forecasting and visibility of upcoming milestones and decision points
  • Produce program-level schedule reporting for governance forums, Steering Committees and executive stakeholders

You will be an experienced Master Scheduler, Program Scheduler or Senior Project Scheduler with a background supporting large-scale, complex technology transformation programs.

  • Confidence working directly with Program Managers, Project Managers, technical leads and third-party vendors

job.title: Associate Utilities Commissioners
job.description:
• Shape the future of essential utility regulation in the NT
  • Bring practical judgement to complex regulatory issues
  • Make a high-impact contribution in a flexible, part-time role

The Utilities Commission of the Northern Territory is a statutory authority established under the Utilities Commission Act 2000 and is the independent economic regulator for the Northern Territory. The Commission is constituted by the Utilities Commissioner and Associate Commissioners and has responsibility across regulated industries, including electricity, ports, water and sewerage.

The object of the Utilities Commission Act 2000 is to establish an economic regulatory framework that promotes and safeguards competition and fair and efficient market conduct. The Commission’s primary purpose is to protect the long-term interests of Territory consumers of services provided by regulated industries, particularly in relation to price, reliability and quality. Its vision is to benefit Territorians through effective regulation, well-informed and transparent decision-making and robust, independent advice.

Planned succession has created two Associate Utilities Commissioner opportunities for experienced professionals to contribute to the Commission’s next chapter and to the effective regulation of essential services for Territorians. Working with the Commissioner, the Associate Utilities Commissioners will contribute to regulatory decisions, strategic direction and oversight of the Commission’s work.

These are flexible, part-time appointments of approximately one day per week. The role is to:

  • support the Utilities Commissioner to deliver the Commission’s statutory functions, and set and achieve the Commission’s strategy and priorities
  • contribute expertise to, and be part of, the Commission’s collective decision-making and advice provision
  • engage with Ministers, government officials, regulated entities, consumers, industry and other regulators, including through meetings and site visits
  • support, and contribute to the development of, Commission staff
  • uphold, and foster a positive culture consistent with, the Commission’s values.

This is an active and hands-on role. The Associate Utilities Commissioners will be expected to understand complex issues, identify key considerations, provide guidance to staff and contribute constructively to regulatory approaches and decisions. The role also involves direct engagement with CEOs, boards, Ministers and other senior stakeholders.

While the role is part-time, it requires flexibility to review detailed material and respond to matters within agreed timeframes outside regular meetings and requires periodic travel to the Northern Territory. Travel is expected to be approximately once per quarter, primarily to Darwin, with the possibility of one annual visit to a regional area outside Darwin.

To be considered for this role, you will bring substantial experience in economic regulation, water or energy regulation, regulated utilities, government policy, law, economics, consulting or a related field. Your experience will be practical and applied, with the judgement to translate complex regulatory, commercial and policy issues into clear advice and decisions.

Your experience may have been gained as a regulator, economist, lawyer, senior executive, consultant, board member or leader within a regulated business. You will be comfortable operating at Commissioner level while engaging sufficiently in detail to support a small specialist team.

You will bring independence, sound judgement and the confidence to express clear views, together with a collaborative approach to working with fellow Commissioners, staff and stakeholders. A high level of integrity, objectivity and professionalism is fundamental.

Candidates must be available for periodic travel to the Northern Territory and able to accommodate a flexible part-time commitment. The appointments are expected to commence in late 2026 or early 2027, subject to relevant approval processes.

job.title: Senior Change Analyst / Change Manager
job.description:
Senior Change Analyst / Change Manager | Works & Asset Management Transformation

Davidson has partnered with Barwon Water to appoint a Senior Change Analyst / Change Manager to support the next phase of one of regional Victoria’s most significant transformation programs.

Barwon Water delivers water, sewerage and recycled water services to more than 330,000 people across the Geelong region and surrounding communities. Through its Works & Asset Management (WAM) transformation, the organisation is investing in new systems, processes and ways of working that will strengthen how it manages its assets and operations into the future.

About the Role

This is a hands-on change delivery role supporting the WAM transformation, helping impacted teams understand, prepare for and successfully adopt new systems, processes and ways of working.

This role requires someone who can quickly understand an existing program, build strong relationships and proactively identify what needs to happen. You'll be comfortable asking difficult questions, investigating issues, challenging assumptions and ensuring change risks aren't allowed to quietly become business problems.

The position is based in Geelong, with an expectation of three days per week onsite and is an initial contract through to the end of June 2027.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and deliver practical change and business readiness activities.
  • Complete stakeholder analysis, change impact assessments and readiness assessments.
  • Identify adoption risks, resistance and process impacts and develop practical responses.
  • Build strong relationships across corporate, technology, engineering and operational teams.
  • Support training, communications, stakeholder engagement and leader activation activities.
  • Coordinate go-live readiness and support post-implementation adoption.

About You

You're a hands-on change professional who enjoys being close to the business and making change happen. You'll be comfortable working independently, asking difficult questions and engaging stakeholders ranging from frontline operational teams through to senior leaders.

Must-Haves

  • Strong hands-on change management experience within complex transformation programs.
  • Experience across change impacts, stakeholder engagement, readiness and adoption.
  • Experience delivering technology-enabled change involving new systems and processes.
  • Strong facilitation, communication and stakeholder management skills.

Nice to Have

  • Experience within utilities, water, infrastructure, asset management or another operational environment.
  • Exposure to ERP, Works & Asset Management or Enterprise Asset Management transformations.

Benefits & Why Barwon Water

This is an opportunity to join a significant transformation program at an important stage of delivery, with the ability to make a tangible impact on how new systems and processes are understood and adopted across Barwon Water.

You'll work across a genuinely diverse stakeholder environment spanning corporate, technology, engineering and frontline operational teams, giving you exposure to the different ways enterprise change impacts people across an organisation.

For someone who enjoys being hands-on, building relationships and turning change plans into practical outcomes, this role offers the opportunity to take meaningful ownership of change delivery through the next phase of the WAM transformation.

Apply Now

job.title: Cyber Security Engineer
job.description:
About the Company

Davidson Technology are working with a State Government Department to secure an experienced Cyber Security Engineer to oversee the technical delivery of critical technical uplift supporting various Cyber initiatives and projects


About the Role

As a Cyber Security Engineer, you will lead the hands-on technical delivery of complex cyber security uplift initiatives, with a particular focus on improving Essential Eight maturity and strengthening the organisation’s overall security posture. You will independently undertake discovery, design and implementation activities including introducing multi-factor authentication across legacy applications and systems, optimising Microsoft Sentinel and expanding security logging, delivering Essential Eight uplift activities, decommissioning legacy technologies, and improving business continuity, high availability and backup capabilities. You will develop technical designs, configurations, implementation plans, procedures and status reporting, navigating ICT governance processes to secure approval and ensure solutions are successfully implemented. Working across multiple technical teams and workstreams, you will coordinate resources and technical change activities, manage dependencies, identify and mitigate technical risks and gaps, and ensure committed scope and timeframes are achieved. You will build strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders, provide technical guidance and coaching to other resources, apply evidence-based analysis and sound judgement to complex security challenges, and support additional cyber security initiatives as required.


About You

To be successful, you will bring strong hands-on technical expertise to deliver complex cyber security initiatives, ensuring technical milestones, deliverables and project outcomes are achieved within agreed timeframes. You will have demonstrated experience implementing security capabilities such as Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) and SIEM/logging solutions using Microsoft Sentinel, complemented by knowledge of the Essential Eight and ISO 27001 security frameworks. You will ideally bring broad technical capability across Microsoft 365 and Azure, Microsoft security products, virtualisation technologies, hybrid cloud and on-premises environments, Active Directory, Group Policy and Windows 11. You will actively contribute to technical workshops, project meetings and risk management activities, proactively identifying potential barriers and keeping stakeholders informed of progress, risks and dependencies. Your strong analytical, problem-solving and communication skills will enable you to work effectively across technical teams, while your ability to produce clear system documentation, processes and procedures in accordance with organisational policies will support secure, governed and sustainable technology outcomes.


The Benefits

You will be offered a 9-month contract (possible 12-month extension) on an excellent hourly rate and the ability to negotiate a flexible working arrangement for the duration of the assignment.

job.title: Project Manager, Cyber Security
job.description:
About the Company

Davidson Technology are working with a large State Government Department to secure a Project Manager, Cyber Security, who will deliver information security solutions to support modern service delivery.


About the Role

As a Project Manager – Cyber Security, you will be responsible for leading the end-to-end delivery of critical cyber security initiatives, with a particular focus on Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), supporting the organisation’s broader security uplift and modern service delivery objectives. Reporting to the Project Director, you will manage projects in accordance with the department’s formal project management methodologies and best-practice guidelines, ensuring agreed scope, timeframes, budgets, quality standards and strategic outcomes are achieved. You will provide strategic advice and input into project deliverables to ensure alignment with departmental strategies and architecture, while proactively monitoring project performance, risks, issues, dependencies and financials. You will lead and mentor project team members, build strong relationships with technical, business and executive stakeholders, and ensure stakeholders remain appropriately informed and engaged throughout the project lifecycle. Through clear and timely reporting, written submissions, briefs, presentations and information papers, you will provide senior stakeholders with the insights required to make informed decisions and successfully navigate complex cyber security delivery challenges.


About You

To be successful in this role, you’ll bring proven experience delivering large-scale, complex cyber security projects within highly regulated enterprise environments, supported by a broad understanding of cyber security domains and the ability to develop robust business cases for security investment. You will ideally have hands-on project delivery experience across Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) implementation, integration and migration, including technologies such as RSA SecurID and Microsoft Entra ID, together with strong knowledge of identity and access management, directory services and security foundations. You will apply established project management methodologies, preferably PRINCE2, to deliver outcomes in accordance with departmental standards and processes, while promoting effective project management practices across multidisciplinary teams. You will demonstrate exceptional stakeholder relationship management, negotiation, consultation and influencing skills, enabling you to engage senior stakeholders, facilitate business change and navigate complex delivery environments. Your experience leading and mentoring multidisciplinary teams, combined with strong analytical, conceptual and problem-solving capability, will enable you to manage competing priorities and successfully deliver cyber security initiatives that strengthen identity security and meet mandatory compliance and maturity requirements such as IS18. Experience operating within complex hospital or healthcare environments and understanding how identity and access controls contribute to safe, secure and uninterrupted healthcare delivery will be highly regarded.

job.title: Executive Director Quality, Risk & Compliance – MannaCare
job.description:
• Executive leadership across quality, clinical governance, enterprise risk and compliance
  • Provide trusted assurance and advice to the CEO, Executive Leadership Team and Board
  • Registered Nurse with current AHPRA registration essential | Doncaster

MannaCare is a purpose led, community anchored aged care provider supporting residents and clients across Melbourne’s eastern suburbs, predominately within the Manningham area. With a clear commitment to dignity, connection and wellbeing, MannaCare delivers a continuum of services spanning residential aged care, respite, specialist dementia support, and tailored community-based services that enable people to live safely and independently for longer. Guided by its iCARE values of Integrity, Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, and Excellence, MannaCare is recognised for a warm, person-centred approach and a genuine focus on quality, safety and continuous improvement in everything it does.

MannaCare is now seeking an Executive Director – Quality, Risk & Compliance to take organisation-wide responsibility for the systems and frameworks that underpin safe, accountable and high-quality care. Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer and joining the Executive Leadership Team, the role brings together quality, clinical governance, safeguarding, compliance, enterprise risk and assurance across Residential Aged Care and Community Services.

A key part of the remit will be providing the CEO, Executive and Board with clear and independent oversight of MannaCare’s risk and assurance environment. As executive custodian of the Enterprise Risk Management Framework, you will maintain oversight across strategic, operational, clinical, financial, people, cyber, compliance and reputational risk, while working with leaders across the organisation to strengthen risk ownership, controls and accountability.

Alongside this, you will lead MannaCare’s approach to clinical governance, safeguarding and regulatory compliance, including accreditation and registration, audit and assurance, incidents and complaints, SIRS and continuous improvement. A key focus will be developing MannaCare’s Quality Framework and defining the ‘MannaCare Way’, establishing a clear and consistent approach to quality across the organisation. Importantly, this is not a role that operates at arm’s length. You will work closely with operational leaders to understand what is happening across services, identify emerging issues and use evidence, trends and organisational insights to drive practical and sustained improvement.

To be successful, you will be a Registered Nurse with current AHPRA registration and bring extensive quality experience gained within aged care or the broader health sector. You will have a strong working knowledge of aged care legislation, regulation and accreditation requirements, together with experience across clinical governance, audit and risk. Just as important will be your ability to exercise sound judgement, constructively challenge when required and build credible relationships from frontline teams through to the Board.

job.title: Sleep Expert & Store Manager
job.description:
The best salespeople don't think of themselves as salespeople. They think of themselves as experts who are here to help.

There are few things more important to someone's wellbeing than sleep. At Sleepy's, our Store Managers and teams take the time to understand what's getting in the way of a better night's sleep and help customers find the right solution.

It's why customers choose us — not because we discount harder, but because our advice is genuine.

Davidson is proudly partnering with Sleepy's to find our next Sleep Expert & Store Manager.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You'll be on the floor selling alongside your team, coaching them to improve and taking ownership of your store's people, culture and commercial performance.

Who this is right for

You'll probably be someone who:

  1. Genuinely loves selling and still wants to be on the floor
  2. Gets energy from coaching people and watching them improve
  3. Loves becoming an expert so you can genuinely help customers
  4. Enjoys the commercial side of running a business
  5. Is always looking for a better way to do things
  6. Wants to lead, not simply manage

Maybe you're already doing more than your job title suggests

If your current leader sees you as simply a store location and a set of numbers but your team knows how much you give to make that store successful, then we should chat?

You're the person coaching them, keeping everyone motivated, solving problems and you still love customer interactions - in fact you’re the best salesperson in the team.

If that sounds familiar, we'd like to hear from you.

At Sleepy's, we want our Store Managers to feel as valued as the customers and teams they look after.

If you spend every day trying to make a difference to other people's lives, we'd like the opportunity to make a difference to yours.

You don't need to come from bedding. Furniture, jewellery, automotive, real estate, wellness, premium retail and more — if customers need to trust you before making an important decision, you'll understand what makes this role different.

We can teach you mattresses. We can't teach curiosity, care and the drive to be excellent.

If that sounds like you, we want to hear from you.

job.title: Executive Assistant to CEO
job.description:
Davidson is proud to partner with Alliance Airlines in the appointment of an experienced Executive Assistant to support its new Chief Executive Officer.

This is a significant opportunity for a highly accomplished Executive Assistant who understands what it takes to operate alongside a CEO in a complex, fast moving and highly visible environment.

This role goes well beyond traditional diary and administrative support. You will become a trusted partner to the CEO, taking ownership of the rhythm and effectiveness of the Office of the CEO and helping ensure their time, attention and focus are directed towards the priorities that matter most.

About Alliance Airlines

Alliance Airlines is one of Australia’s leading aviation services businesses, delivering specialised aviation solutions across charter, fly in fly out and scheduled services.

Operating within a complex and highly regulated environment, Alliance has built a strong reputation for operational excellence, safety and service.

With a new CEO commencing, this appointment represents an opportunity to join the business at an important point in its journey and establish a highly effective working partnership from the outset.

About the Role

As Executive Assistant to the CEO, you will provide high level, confidential executive support while taking genuine ownership of the day to day operation of the CEO’s office.

Your role will be to anticipate, prioritise and coordinate. You will understand what requires the CEO’s attention, what can be delegated, what needs to happen next and how to keep priorities moving without requiring constant direction.

Key responsibilities will include:

  • Owning the CEO’s complex diary and proactively managing competing priorities, meetings and commitments
  • Ensuring the CEO is prepared for meetings with the appropriate agendas, papers, briefings and background information
  • Managing domestic and international travel, including detailed itineraries, logistics and changes at short notice
  • Coordinating Executive Leadership Team meetings and other senior executive forums
  • Preparing executive correspondence, presentations, reports and internal communications
  • Maintaining actions and following up priorities across the business to ensure commitments are delivered
  • Acting as a key point of contact between the CEO, Executive Leadership Team, Board stakeholders, customers, suppliers and external partners
  • Supporting CEO communications, employee engagement activity and corporate events
  • Managing confidential and sensitive matters with a high level of discretion and judgement
  • Providing project support to the CEO as required, with the scope and complexity of projects increasing over time
  • Helping maintain a highly organised, considered and professional Office of the CEO

The role operates across a broad range of commercial, operational and corporate priorities, often with changing timelines. You will need to be comfortable making judgement calls, challenging competing demands when appropriate and identifying potential issues before they become problems.

About You

We are looking for an experienced Executive Assistant who has already operated at CEO, C Suite or Board level and understands the judgement, maturity and discretion required at this level.

You will ideally bring:

  • A minimum of five years experience within senior executive support, with demonstrated experience supporting CEO, C Suite or Board level stakeholders
  • Exceptional complex diary management and prioritisation capability
  • The confidence to manage access to a CEO and professionally navigate competing stakeholder demands
  • Strong judgement and the ability to make informed decisions without needing constant direction
  • Exceptional written communication skills with experience preparing executive level correspondence and communications
  • Experience coordinating complex domestic and international travel
  • Strong meeting management, minute taking and action tracking capability
  • Advanced capability across Microsoft Office 365, particularly Outlook, Word and PowerPoint
  • An interest in using technology and AI enabled tools to improve efficiency and ways of working
  • The ability to remain composed, organised and solutions focused when priorities change quickly
  • Absolute discretion when working with confidential commercial, executive and people matters

Most importantly, you will be proactive by nature. You will notice what needs attention, take ownership and follow through. You will be comfortable working with a CEO who expects their EA to think ahead, have an opinion, identify better ways of operating and create structure around a demanding executive workload.

The Benefits

  • Opportunity to partner directly with the new CEO of Alliance Airlines
  • Highly visible role with exposure across the Executive Leadership Team and broader business
  • Genuine ownership over the operation and effectiveness of the Office of the CEO
  • Broad exposure across executive priorities, communications, stakeholder engagement and projects
  • Opportunity to establish a strong working partnership with the CEO from the beginning of their tenure

job.title: Chief Financial Officer
job.description:
Davidson is partnering with Anglican Church Southern Queensland (ACSQ) to appoint an Executive Director, Finance & Diocesan Services Commission, a pivotal executive leadership role responsible for the financial stewardship and long-term sustainability of one of Queensland's largest and most diverse faith-based organisations.

ACSQ operates across a complex portfolio of parishes, schools, property, community services and ministry operations, with annual revenue exceeding $500 million and investment assets of more than $300 million.

job.description:
Lead the store. Develop the team. Help customers sleep better.

Sleepy’s is one of Australia’s most respected specialist bedding retailers, built on trust, expertise and a genuinely different approach to customer service.

Davidson is proudly partnering with Sleepy’s to appoint a sales-driven Store Manager who loves being on the floor, developing people and delivering results.

About the role

This is not a back-office management role.

You’ll be an active salesperson who leads by example – building rapport, asking great questions and understanding what the customer really needs before recommending a solution.

You’ll also coach your team to do the same.

You will:

  • Lead from the floor and personally contribute to sales.
  • Coach and develop your team through real customer interactions.
  • Build exceptional product knowledge and create genuine sleep experts.
  • Drive sales, conversion, margin and customer experience.
  • Create a positive, team-first culture where success is shared.
  • Take ownership of store presentation, merchandising and performance.
  • Identify opportunities to continually improve the customer journey.
  • Build relationships within the local community to generate new opportunities.

About you

Above everything else, you genuinely enjoy selling.

You’re commercially hungry but humble, naturally curious about people and confident asking questions to uncover what a customer really needs.

You’re also:

  • An authentic relationship builder who earns trust quickly.
  • Confident asking for the sale without being pushy.
  • A hands-on leader who coaches by example.
  • Energised by targets, improvement and developing others.
  • Team-focused rather than individually competitive.
  • Curious, adaptable and always looking to learn.
  • Resilient enough to reset quickly after a missed sale and focus on the next customer.

Your background could be in bedding, furniture, jewellery, automotive, real estate, health, wellness, premium retail or another consultative sales environment.

We can teach you mattresses and sleep products.

What we’re looking for is the sales instinct, curiosity, empathy and leadership capability that are much harder to teach.

What’s on offer

  • Strong base salary plus attractive incentive opportunity.
  • Specialist training in sales, leadership, products and sleep health.
  • Support from an accessible and genuinely invested leadership team.
  • The autonomy to lead and improve your store.
  • Career development within a growing national retailer.
  • The opportunity to sell something that genuinely improves people’s lives.

At Sleepy’s, we’re not simply selling someone a bed.

We’re helping them buy a better night’s sleep.

If you’re a strong salesperson who loves developing people and wants to lead from the front, we want to hear from you.

job.title: AO5 Document Controller
job.description:

The Department of Transport and Main Roads (TMR) is focused on creating a single integrated transport network accessible to everyone and making a positive difference to the lives of Queenslanders.

Queensland’s passenger rail network is undergoing significant transformation, with major infrastructure investment planned to support population growth and future transport demands.

The Logan and Gold Coast Faster Rail Project forms a key part of this investment. The $5.75 billion project will deliver extensive track upgrades, eight new train stations, five level crossing removals, park ‘n’ ride upgrades and new active travel pathways across a 20km corridor.

TMR fosters an inclusive workplace culture, supports career development and work-life balance, and is committed to reconciliation and creating opportunities for Aboriginal peoples and Torres Strait Islander peoples to thrive.


About the Role

Reporting to the Project Controls Office Manager, you will join the Project Document Control team and support the successful delivery of the Logan and Gold Coast Faster Rail Project. As Advisor (Document Control), you will help ensure the accuracy, quality and integrity of project documentation while maintaining compliance with regulatory requirements, contractual obligations and internal procedures.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Reviewing and coordinating updates to Project Document Control Management Plans and procedures.
  • Managing document workflows, reviews, approvals, tracking and quality checks across complex project documentation.

About You

Previous experience using InEight Document (TeamBinder) is mandatory.

Experience working within a major project environment will be highly regarded. You will bring a strong understanding of document management processes, quality control and governance, together with the ability to work collaboratively with a broad range of project stakeholders.

The Benefits

The Infrastructure Services Division within the Queensland Department of Education manages approximately $2 billion in annual infrastructure investment and a $40 billion asset base, supporting the delivery of quality education infrastructure and services across Queensland.

The Transformation Management Office (TMO) provides governance, coordination and oversight of the Business Transformation Portfolio, driving improvements in governance, asset lifecycle management, financial oversight and organisational capability.

job.description:
Agile Delivery Manager

Do you have experience stepping into a low-maturity technology environment and quickly establishing the delivery practices, standards and accountability needed to get teams operating effectively? Apply now!

Western Suburbs | Competitive Daily Rate | 9-Month Initial Contract

Our client, a well-established national organisation, is seeking an experienced Agile Delivery Manager for an initial 9-month contract to strengthen delivery capability within its internal technology function.

The organisation is currently undertaking a significant enterprise transformation centred around Microsoft Dynamics 365. While an external Systems Integrator is responsible for the core D365 implementation, there is a need to establish stronger delivery disciplines, standards and ways of working across the internal technology team.

This isn't a traditional Project Manager or Scrum Master role. We're looking for someone who has built delivery capability rather than inherited it – Someone comfortable entering an environment where processes, documentation, planning and ways of working aren't yet mature and putting the right foundations in place.

Your responsibilities will include but not be limited to:

  • Assess the current delivery environment and quickly identify gaps across processes, governance, planning, documentation, tooling and accountability.
  • Establish practical Agile delivery practices and standards using Scrum, Kanban and fit-for-purpose approaches appropriate to the team's maturity.
  • Improve visibility of work through Azure DevOps, ensuring priorities, ownership, progress, dependencies and blockers are clearly understood.
  • Introduce stronger disciplines around requirements, technical designs, approvals, documentation and agreed definitions of "done".
  • Coach and influence internal technology teams to adopt stronger delivery behaviours, challenging existing practices and driving accountability where required.
  • Work alongside technology leadership, business stakeholders and the Systems Integrator to embed sustainable practices while maintaining momentum across the transformation.

Skills and experience – To be successful in this role, you will bring:

  • Demonstrated experience establishing delivery practices and standards within a low-maturity technology environment.
  • Strong Agile delivery experience across Scrum, Kanban and Azure DevOps.
  • Experience introducing structure and delivery discipline while significant technology initiatives are already underway.
  • Strong stakeholder influence, with the confidence to challenge existing practices and drive accountability.

Nice to haves:

  • ERP or enterprise application transformation experience, ideally Microsoft Dynamics 365.
  • Experience working alongside external Systems Integrators.

This is an initial 9-month contract with a competitive daily rate, based in Melbourne's Western Suburbs with a minimum of three days onsite per week and a preference for four.

You'll have the opportunity to make a tangible impact by establishing the delivery foundations, standards and ways of working that will strengthen both the immediate transformation and the broader technology function.

job.title: Senior Workday Procurement & Strategic Supporting Consultant
job.description:
JOB OVERVIEW:

About the Role

We are seeking a Senior Workday Procurement & Strategic Sourcing Support Consultant to provide ongoing functional and production support across Workday Procurement, Supplier Accounts, Inventory Management and Strategic Sourcing.

You will play a key role in maintaining critical procurement operations, supporting supplier onboarding and management, resolving production issues, managing sourcing activities and contracts, and contributing to continuous improvement across the Workday ecosystem.

This role is ideal for a senior Workday specialist with deep functional expertise across Procurement and Strategic Sourcing, combined with strong experience supporting complex production environments and supplier integrations.

Key Responsibilities:

Workday Procurement

  • Support requisitions, purchase orders and goods/services procurement processes.
  • Troubleshoot procurement business processes, approvals, receiving and receipt issues.
  • Resolve functional and user support issues.

Supplier Management & Accounts

  • Support supplier onboarding, maintenance and change requests.
  • Resolve supplier invoice, payment, statement and reconciliation issues.
  • Support invoice processing and matching exceptions.
  • Coordinate vendor master governance activities.

Strategic Sourcing

  • Support RFx and bidding events, supplier questionnaires and evaluations.
  • Maintain sourcing templates and support award recommendations.
  • Provide sourcing reporting and analytics.

Contract Management

  • Support sourcing contracts and contract lifecycle activities.
  • Manage contract amendments, renewals and reporting.

Inventory Management
