  • Assist with inventory reconciliations and reporting.

Supplier Integration Support

  • Work closely with integration teams to troubleshoot supplier connectivity issues.
  • Support Punchout suppliers, supplier catalogues and cXML/PO transmission.
  • Monitor and troubleshoot invoice interfaces.

Reporting & Continuous Improvement

  • Support procurement and sourcing reporting and analytics.
  • Maintain support procedures and contribute to enhancement releases.
  • Identify process improvement opportunities.
  • Perform impact assessments for Workday updates.

Security

  • Support user provisioning, role assignments and domain security.
  • Assist with security policy changes, Segregation of Duties reviews and periodic access reviews.
  • Support new security design and change requests.

About You

  • 7+ years of Workday Procurement experience.
  • Strong hands-on experience with Workday Strategic Sourcing.
  • Strong knowledge of requisitions, POs, Supplier Accounts, Inventory, Contracts and Strategic Sourcing.
  • Extensive supplier management experience.
  • Experience supporting supplier integrations and production environments.
  • Strong reporting and analytical capabilities.
  • Excellent stakeholder communication and problem-solving skills.

Desirable Experience

  • Workday Strategic Sourcing certification.
  • Procurement transformation experience.
  • Supplier enablement experience.
  • Punchout and cXML experience.
  • Utilities industry experience.

Why This Opportunity?

  • Work across a large-scale Workday ecosystem with multiple modules.
  • Support a complex production environment spanning cloud and third-party platforms.
  • Collaborate with Finance, Procurement, Payroll, Projects and Technology stakeholders.
  • Contribute to ongoing optimisation and continuous improvement.
  • Join a long-term consulting engagement through the end of April 2027.

job.title: AO7 Principal Advisor
job.description:
About the Company

This Queensland Government environment is responsible for supporting the effective operation of road networks across the state. With a strong focus on sound governance, evidence-based decision-making and continuous improvement, the team works across operational and strategic priorities to deliver practical outcomes for Queensland’s road network.

About the Role

As Principal Advisor, you will coordinate, lead and support the development and delivery of evidence-based policy, guidelines, processes and strategic advice supporting road network operations.

You will provide insights that inform strategy, enhance decision-making and drive continuous improvement, while ensuring relevant government and departmental legislation and policy directives are appropriately applied.

Key projects will include reviewing the stationary and abandoned vehicle management policy framework, reviewing road network operations imagery and audio policy frameworks, and overseeing a request-for-information function involving road network operations imagery.

Your responsibilities will also include developing and maintaining strategies and policy frameworks, identifying and scoping business requirements, and contributing to departmental process and system initiatives. You will prepare high-quality reports, briefs, submissions, research papers and strategic advice for senior and executive management.

A key part of the role will be building effective stakeholder networks and managing complex, sensitive, political and high-risk matters to achieve timely and practical resolutions.

About You

You will bring strong tactical or operational policy experience gained within a government environment, with demonstrated capability across the policy lifecycle. Importantly, you understand how to balance operational realities with fit-for-purpose governance and policy practice.

You will ideally demonstrate:

  • Experience developing and implementing operational policy, strategies and governance frameworks
  • Knowledge and practical application of Queensland information privacy law and information privacy program management
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills and the ability to work collaboratively across teams to achieve balanced and tangible business outcomes
  • Experience preparing high-quality strategic advice, briefs, reports, submissions and research papers
  • Instructional design or technical training experience, including developing accessible learning materials that translate complex policies, processes and work instructions
  • The ability to navigate complex, sensitive and potentially high-risk stakeholder matters
  • Road network operations or public transport operations experience will be highly regarded

You will also bring a professional and collaborative approach, with the ability to share knowledge, mentor colleagues and contribute positively to team capability.

The Benefits

This AO7 opportunity offers the chance to contribute to significant policy and operational initiatives with statewide impact.

The successful candidate can be based in Brisbane or Bundaberg, Queensland. Candidates based in Bundaberg will be required to travel to operational facilities, including Brisbane and Nerang, as required.

You will have the opportunity to work across complex policy, privacy and operational matters while engaging with senior stakeholders and contributing directly to the future planning and operation of Queensland’s road network.

job.title: Data Analytics & Engineering Specialist
job.description:
Data Specialist – Microsoft Data & Analytics

Brisbane | Permanent | $120,000 – $140,000 + Super

Join a growing Australian organisation and take ownership of a modern data environment as it moves into its next stage of maturity.

Our client is a large, privately owned Australian business with a significant national footprint and operations across multiple locations. Over the past 12 months, they have invested heavily in establishing a modern Microsoft data platform. With the foundations now in place, they are looking for an experienced Data Specialist to help build trusted, scalable data models and unlock greater value from data across the organisation.

This is not a traditional reporting or dashboard-focused position. The role is approximately 70–80% data, modelling and problem-solving, with Power BI and reporting making up the balance.

The Role

Working closely with the Group Manager – Data & Analytics, you will operate across the data lifecycle and take ownership of complex data challenges.

You will work with data coming from multiple operational, financial, customer and business systems, bringing different structures and definitions together into consistent and trusted enterprise datasets.

Key responsibilities will include:

  • Designing dimensional models, star schemas, facts and dimensions
  • Building and maintaining trusted semantic models for enterprise reporting
  • Developing complex SQL queries, transformations and reusable data structures
  • Integrating and standardising data from multiple source systems
  • Investigating data discrepancies and reconciling conflicting numbers across systems and reports
  • Working with historical data and differing source-system structures
  • Developing and supporting ingestion and transformation pipelines
  • Improving query, model and reporting performance
  • Building reusable datasets rather than report-specific solutions
  • Developing Power BI reports and DAX where required
  • Supporting source control, testing, DevOps and CI/CD practices
  • Working directly with business SMEs to understand how underlying systems and data behave

The environment is predominantly Microsoft and includes Microsoft Fabric, OneLake, Data Warehouse, Azure Data Factory, SQL, Power BI/DAX and Azure DevOps.

About You

We're looking for someone who is technically strong but, equally importantly, curious and investigative.

You'll be comfortable questioning requirements, challenging assumptions and independently working through complex data problems. If two systems produce different numbers, you'll want to understand why rather than simply changing the report.

Ideally, you will bring:

  • Advanced SQL development and query optimisation skills
  • Strong dimensional and semantic modelling experience
  • Excellent understanding of star schemas, facts, dimensions and data grain
  • Experience integrating complex data from multiple source systems
  • Strong data reconciliation, validation and data-quality capability
  • Power BI experience, including semantic models and DAX
  • Experience with modern data warehouse or lakehouse environments
  • Understanding of ETL/ELT and data pipeline orchestration
  • Exposure to Git, DevOps and structured deployment practices
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills

Experience with Microsoft Fabric, Azure Data Factory, Data Vault, Python/PySpark or Azure DevOps would be advantageous, but we won't overlook an excellent data modeller simply because you've worked with another modern platform such as Databricks or Snowflake.

Experience within retail, automotive, FMCG or another multi-site/multi-entity organisation would also be highly regarded.

Why Consider This Opportunity?

This is an opportunity to join an organisation where the core architecture has been established, but there is still significant scope to influence how the data capability develops.

You'll have genuine ownership, work across a diverse national business and see the direct impact of the solutions you build. Rather than being confined to one narrow part of the data stack, you'll have the opportunity to work across engineering, modelling, semantic layers, data quality and reporting.

For someone who enjoys solving difficult data problems and wants to help build a trusted enterprise data capability over the long term, this is an excellent opportunity.

job.title: Manager People, Safety & Customer Experience - City of Wodonga
job.description:
• Influence organisational performance in a key leadership role
  • Lead workforce strategy, enterprise bargaining and HR transformation
  • Join a high performing and future focused Council

The City of Wodonga is a progressive and community-focused regional Council, recognised for its commitment to innovation, service excellence and sustainable growth. Located in north-east Victoria on the Murray River and forming part of the dynamic Albury-Wodonga region, Wodonga combines the lifestyle and connectivity of a major regional centre with easy access to Victoria’s High Country, renowned food and wine regions and outstanding natural environments. With a strong focus on accountability, continuous improvement and delivering value for its community, Council offers a collaborative and forward-thinking environment where leaders can make a meaningful contribution to both the organisation and the wider community.

Reporting to the Director Corporate, the Manager People, Safety and Customer Experience is a key leadership position responsible for shaping and delivering contemporary people, safety and customer strategies across Council. You will provide trusted, commercially focused advice to the Executive Leadership Team while leading key priorities including enterprise bargaining, strengthening workforce planning, evolving the HR business partnering model and continuing to mature Council’s approach to health, safety and wellbeing. With a strong focus on organisational performance, you will use data and insights to inform decision-making, strengthen capability and lead change and continuous improvement across the portfolio.

To be considered for this role, you will be a contemporary and commercially minded people leader with strong experience across employee and industrial relations, workforce strategy and organisational change. Your background could come from local government, the broader public sector or a complex service-based organisation, with a proven ability to navigate sophisticated stakeholder, governance and industrial environments. An influential communicator with strong judgement, you will be comfortable advising senior executives and balancing workforce considerations with broader organisational priorities. Data-oriented and outcomes focused, you will bring the strategic capability to modernise the People function alongside the leadership breadth to oversee safety and customer experience within a complex and politically nuanced environment.

job.title: Senior DMS & SharePoint Administrator
job.description:
Senior DMS & SharePoint Administrator

Location: Melbourne, VIC
Duration: 3 months
Start: Immediate

We are seeking an experienced Senior DMS & SharePoint Administrator to support a major SharePoint Online Document Management System (DMS) implementation, transition and optimisation initiative.
This is a hands-on senior specialist role suited to someone with strong enterprise-level experience across SharePoint Online, Microsoft 365, Power Platform and information governance.

About the Role

You will be responsible for the technical administration, configuration, security, governance and continuous improvement of a SharePoint Online-based enterprise DMS.
Working closely with ICT, Records Management, business stakeholders and external vendors, you will support the successful implementation, migration, adoption and transition of the DMS into business-as-usual operations.

Key Responsibilities

  • Administer and optimise SharePoint Online, including sites, libraries, hub structures, metadata, content types, term stores, navigation and information architecture.
  • Manage and support Microsoft 365 services, including Teams, OneDrive, Power Automate, Power Apps and Microsoft Purview.
  • Develop and maintain Power Automate workflows supporting document management, approvals, reviews, notifications and compliance processes.
  • Manage permissions, security groups, access controls, retention settings and information governance requirements.
  • Support Microsoft Purview configuration, retention policies, lifecycle controls and records management.
  • Provide technical oversight for DMS migrations, including mapping, testing, validation, reconciliation, exception reporting and remediation.
  • Monitor and resolve data quality issues including metadata gaps, duplicate content, broken links and access anomalies.
  • Provide Level 2/3 technical support and troubleshoot complex SharePoint, Microsoft 365, workflow, permissions and integration issues.
  • Prepare technical documentation, procedures, user guides, training materials and governance artefacts.
  • Support user adoption through training, workshops and stakeholder engagement.
  • Identify opportunities to improve DMS usability, automation, governance, reporting and overall platform efficiency.

About You

We are looking for a senior SharePoint/Microsoft 365 specialist with:

  • Strong enterprise-level experience administering SharePoint Online and Microsoft 365.
  • Strong knowledge of SharePoint architecture, hub sites, document libraries, content types, managed metadata, term stores, search and information architecture.
  • Experience with an enterprise Document Management System, preferably SharePoint-based.
  • Strong understanding of permissions, security, retention, records management and information governance.
  • Hands-on experience with Power Automate and Power Platform.
  • Experience supporting SharePoint/DMS migration projects, including validation, reconciliation and remediation.
  • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving capability.
  • Excellent stakeholder communication skills and the ability to translate technical concepts into practical business advice.

Desirable

  • Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management / Records Management experience.
  • PowerShell experience for Microsoft 365 and SharePoint administration.
  • Experience with ShareGate or similar SharePoint migration tools.
  • Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Information Protection or Power Platform certifications.
  • Experience with Microsoft 365 Copilot readiness or information governance uplift.

job.title: Senior Project Officer - Governance & Assurance
job.description:
Davidson is partnering with a major Queensland organisation to recruit an experienced Senior Project Officer to join a high performing project environment, with a strong focus on project assurance, governance compliance and quality review.

About the Company

Our client is a large and complex Queensland organisation responsible for delivering critical infrastructure and services across the state.

Within a major capital delivery environment, this team supports the planning and delivery of a significant portfolio of projects, with a strong focus on governance, assurance, risk management and quality outcomes.



About the Role

Working within an established Program Management Office, this role will provide assurance and governance oversight across a broad portfolio of infrastructure projects.

This is an ideal opportunity for someone who enjoys getting into the detail of project documentation, identifying gaps, challenging the quality of information presented and ensuring project papers are ready to progress through formal governance and approval processes.

A key focus of the position will be reviewing project documentation and governance meeting papers before they are issued, ensuring information is accurate, complete and compliant with established project governance requirements.


Your responsibilities will include:

  • Reviewing project papers, agendas, reports, stage gate documentation and supporting materials prior to governance meetings
  • Undertaking assurance reviews to identify gaps, risks, inconsistencies and areas of non compliance
  • Providing constructive feedback to Project Managers and project teams to ensure documentation meets required governance and quality standards
  • Supporting pre gate assurance activities and project progression through established approval processes
  • Monitoring project governance compliance and identifying opportunities to strengthen processes and controls
  • Working closely with Project Managers to ensure governance papers provide clear, accurate and succinct information to support informed decision making
  • Coordinating governance submissions, reports, presentations, agendas and meeting documentation
  • Maintaining governance and assurance registers, systems, processes and tracking mechanisms
  • Building effective relationships with Project Managers, Project Directors, senior leaders and governance stakeholders

About You

We are particularly interested in candidates who bring a strong assurance mindset and are comfortable critically reviewing project information rather than simply coordinating documents.

You will ideally bring:

  • Demonstrated experience within project assurance, governance, audit, compliance or project controls
  • Strong experience reviewing project documentation and identifying gaps, risks, inconsistencies or areas requiring further information
  • Experience undertaking assurance or audit reviews within a project environment
  • The confidence to challenge documentation and provide clear, constructive feedback to Project Managers and senior stakeholders
  • Strong understanding of project governance frameworks, stage gates, approval processes and governance requirements
  • Excellent written communication skills with exceptional attention to detail
  • Experience preparing or reviewing governance papers, reports, submissions and supporting documentation
  • Strong stakeholder management skills with the ability to work across multidisciplinary project teams
  • Intermediate to advanced Microsoft Office skills, particularly Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams and SharePoint


Experience within infrastructure, utilities, government or another complex project delivery environment would be highly regarded.


The Benefits

  • Contract opportunity through to 5 January
  • Flexible hybrid working arrangement with 3 days working from home and 2 days in the office
  • Opportunity to work across a significant portfolio of infrastructure projects
  • Strong exposure to project governance, assurance and senior decision making forums
  • Work closely with experienced Project Managers, Project Directors and senior stakeholders
  • Join an established Program Management Office within a major Queensland organisation

job.title: HR Advisor | Workforce & People
job.description:
HR Advisor | Workforce & People

Katherine West Health Board | Katherine, NT

$94,907 – $116,569 + 12% super | Salary packaging | Relocation support




Make your next HR role mean something.




Are you an experienced HR Advisor looking for broader exposure, greater autonomy and the opportunity to work somewhere your contribution genuinely matters?




Davidson is proud to partner with Katherine West Health Board (KWHB), an Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Organisation providing primary healthcare and health-related programs to Aboriginal communities across approximately 162,000km² of the remote Katherine West region.




KWHB has experienced significant organisational growth and is continuing to strengthen its Human Resources function to support its expanding workforce.




We're now seeking an experienced HR Advisor to join the team in Katherine.




Internally titled Workforce Coordinator, this is a broad, hands-on HR advisory role working closely with the Senior Manager Human Resources and supporting managers and employees across the organisation.




If you enjoy variety, like being close to the action and want the opportunity to develop across the breadth of HR rather than being confined to one specialist area, this could be a fantastic next move.




The opportunity

You'll become a trusted member of a growing HR team, providing practical advice and support across the employee lifecycle.




No two days are likely to look exactly the same.




You'll support managers with day-to-day HR matters, prepare employment documentation, oversee workforce compliance, contribute to HR reporting and process improvement, and help ensure employees joining KWHB have a consistent and culturally appropriate experience.




You'll also have exposure to workplace reviews and investigations, workforce planning and broader organisational improvement initiatives.




Your responsibilities will include:

  • Providing practical HR advice and support to managers and employees
  • Interpreting and applying HR policies, procedures, employment legislation and relevant industrial instruments
  • Preparing contracts, variations, secondments and other employment documentation
  • Supporting recruitment, onboarding, induction and offboarding
  • Monitoring licences, registrations, checks, certifications and other workforce compliance requirements
  • Supporting remuneration changes, pay progression, allowances and contractual changes
  • Maintaining accurate employee records and HR information systems
  • Coordinating workforce logistics including travel, accommodation and remote workforce requirements
  • Preparing workforce reporting and identifying trends, risks and opportunities
  • Contributing to HR policy, procedure and process improvement
  • Supporting workplace reviews and investigations as required
  • Contributing to culturally appropriate induction, orientation and workforce development activities.




    The position also provides an opportunity to support and mentor less experienced HR and administrative team members as the function continues to evolve.




    About you

    We're looking for an experienced HR generalist who is comfortable providing practical advice and doesn't need every answer handed to them.




    You don't need to be the finished product or an ER/IR specialist. You do, however, need enough HR experience and judgement to work through an issue, interpret the relevant policy or legislation, provide sensible advice and recognise when something needs to be escalated.




    You'll ideally bring:
  • Experience at HR Advisor, People & Culture Advisor, Senior HR Coordinator or similar level
  • Practical experience providing HR advice and support to managers
  • Sound knowledge of HR policies, procedures and relevant employment legislation
  • Experience across employment documentation and employee lifecycle processes
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Confidence managing multiple priorities and working autonomously
  • Strong administration, systems and attention to detail
  • Sound judgement, discretion and professionalism
  • A practical, solutions-focused approach
  • The ability to build trusted relationships across a diverse and geographically dispersed workforce.




    Experience in health, community services, government, not-for-profit or an Aboriginal Community Controlled Organisation would be highly regarded, but isn't essential.




    A qualification in Human Resources, Business or a related discipline is desirable rather than mandatory, with equivalent relevant experience also considered.




    Working with Katherine West Health Board

    This role is about more than providing HR advice from behind a desk.




    KWHB supports employees across Katherine and remote Aboriginal communities throughout the Katherine West region. You'll work with people from diverse professional, cultural and community backgrounds and will need to approach those relationships with respect, curiosity and cultural humility.




    KWHB is committed to the recruitment, retention and development of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander employees and to creating culturally safe workplaces where people can develop meaningful careers.




    You'll occasionally travel to remote communities by road and/or light aircraft as part of the role.




    What's on offer?
  • $94,907 – $116,569 + 12% super, negotiable based on relevant skills and experience
  • 6 weeks annual leave + 18% leave loading
  • 2 weeks personal leave
  • Annual CPI increases
  • Salary packaging up to $15,900 per FBT year
  • Meal & Entertainment Card up to $2,650
  • Remote Area Benefits
  • Novated leasing
  • Relocation assistance up to $3,000
  • 6–8 weeks accommodation support on relocation
  • Travel allowance for work-related travel
  • Mobile phone allowance
  • Flexible working arrangements
  • Generous professional development support
  • Strong internal career pathways
  • The opportunity to build a career within a respected Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Organisation.




    Before you apply

    This is a full-time permanent role based in Katherine, Northern Territory.

    The successful candidate will need:
  • A current NT Driver's Licence or the ability to obtain one
  • A current NT Working with Children Clearance (Ochre Card) or ability to obtain
  • A current Criminal History Check or ability to obtain
  • COVID-19 immunisation – minimum one dose
  • High-level computer skills including Microsoft Office and HR information systems
  • The ability and willingness to travel to remote locations by road and/or light aircraft
  • A demonstrated understanding of Aboriginal cultural values and commitment to the advancement and self-determination of Aboriginal communities.




    KWHB is also open to considering suitably experienced candidates already living in Australia on a visa, subject to assessment of individual visa conditions and work rights.




    Candidates across Australia and New Zealand who are genuinely prepared to relocate to Katherine are encouraged to apply.




    Interested?

    If you're an HR Advisor looking for an opportunity that offers breadth, autonomy, purpose and the chance to make a meaningful contribution within a growing organisation, we'd love to hear from you.




    To apply - Please note:




    Due to the quick turnaround for this opportunity and anticipated application volumes, please submit your application directly through the advertised application link rather than emailing your resume to the consultant - This will ensure your application is captured promptly as part of the recruitment process.




    Please apply with current resume in Microsoft Word format only (.doc or .docx) through the application portal. If you would like to have a confidential discussion, please contact Taylah Gurney. Want to know more about Davidson? Visit us at www.davidsonwp.com




    Davidson acknowledges the Traditional Custodians of the lands on which we work and live. We are also committed to equal opportunity and strive to promote diversity, inclusion, belonging, flexibility, and accessibility in all that we do.




    Should you require assistance in your interactions with us or through a recruitment process, please let us know so we can provide adjustments for you.

job.title: Health and Safety Manager
job.description:
2-month contract | 3 days per week | Remote working

About the Company
This purpose-led, national organisation operates across Australia, with employees and stakeholders located across metropolitan, regional and remote environments. The organisation places a strong emphasis on maintaining a positive safety culture and robust health and safety practices.

About the Role
An opportunity is available for an experienced Health and Safety Manager to join the organisation on a part-time contract from 21 September to 20 November 2026, working 3 days per week remotely.

This senior role will be responsible for the delivery and continual improvement of the organisation's national health and safety program. You will provide strategic and technical advice, review and strengthen health and safety systems, policies and procedures, and drive a positive and proactive safety culture across the organisation.

Key responsibilities will include:

  • Providing strategic and technical advice on health and safety legislation, risks and compliance
  • Reviewing and developing health and safety policies, procedures and guidance
  • Driving continuous improvement of health and safety systems and organisational safety culture
  • Preparing health and safety reporting for senior leadership, committees and the Board
  • Supporting incident and near-miss investigations, reporting and recommendations
  • Supporting the organisation's Health and Safety Committee
  • Managing health and safety registers, systems and external service providers
  • Providing advice and support to a geographically dispersed workforce

About You
You will be an experienced health and safety professional who is comfortable operating at both a strategic and hands-on level. You will have the confidence to influence senior stakeholders while providing practical advice and solutions across a diverse organisation.

You will bring:

  • A minimum of 7 years' experience in a senior health and safety position
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications
  • Strong knowledge of health and safety legislation, risk assessment and compliance requirements
  • Practical experience implementing health and safety legislation across multiple Australian jurisdictions
  • Demonstrated experience reviewing and improving safety systems, policies and organisational safety culture
  • Strong leadership, stakeholder management and influencing skills
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Experience supporting health and safety requirements across regional or remote environments
  • A current driver's licence

Experience within the not-for-profit sector would be advantageous.

The Benefits

  • $70-$80 per hour + super
  • 3 days per week
  • Remote working
  • Contract from 21 September to 20 November 2026
  • Senior, organisation-wide health and safety remit
  • Opportunity to lead meaningful improvements across safety systems, culture and practices


Please apply with current resume in Microsoft Word format only (.doc or .docx). If you would like to have a confidential discussion, please contact on chantelle.flood@davidsonwp.com , quoting reference JN -082026-44116. Want to know more about Davidson? Visit us at www.davidsonwp.com

job.title: Environmental and Development Planner
job.description:
Davidson is the proud recruitment partner of SEC Victoria as they accelerate Victoria’s renewable energy transition.

Do work that makes a difference
Join an organisation who’s making a real difference to Victoria's energy future. SEC’s passionate people are working to support the transition to renewable energy and delivering affordable, reliable, renewable energy for all Victorians.

We offer hybrid working with offices in Melbourne’s CBD and Morwell.

What your day could look like
You'll work across SEC's growing portfolio of renewable energy and storage projects, taking ownership of key Environmental & Planning Approvals activities to support projects from development through to delivery. Your day might involve coordinating consultants, reviewing technical reports, contributing to approval submissions, and providing planning and environmental advice to help projects progress through critical milestones and investment decisions.

You'll collaborate with project teams, external advisors, regulators, government agencies, Traditional Owners, First Peoples representatives, and local communities to secure project planning approvals. You will drive effective Stakeholder & Regulatory Engagement. Alongside managing relationships and navigating approval pathways, you'll contribute to Compliance, Risk & Strategic Planning by monitoring regulatory requirements, supporting environmental and planning obligations, identifying emerging risks and opportunities, and helping shape project strategies that deliver successful and sustainable outcomes.

What you need to be successful
You'll bring a combination of planning or environmental expertise, strong stakeholder engagement skills, and the ability to manage competing priorities in a dynamic project environment. With experience achieving environmental and planning approvals, you'll be comfortable working across multiple workstreams, building trusted relationships with diverse stakeholders, and providing practical advice that helps projects progress. Experience in renewable energy, major infrastructure, or similarly complex project environments will help you thrive as SEC continues to grow its portfolio of renewable energy assets.

  • Relevant Qualifications & Technical Expertise - Tertiary qualifications in statutory planning, environmental science, environmental management, or a related discipline, with experience supporting environmental and planning approval processes.
  • Stakeholder Engagement & Communication - Strong relationship-building and communication skills, with the ability to engage and influence a broad range of stakeholders, including consultants, regulators, government agencies, and community representatives.
  • Project Delivery & Commercial Awareness - Proven ability to manage multiple priorities, apply sound judgement, and contribute strategic, commercially minded advice that supports successful project outcomes.

What is it like to work at SEC?
Join a team of passionate, purpose-driven people who care about the work they do and the people they work with. At SEC, their collaborative and inclusive culture means you’ll enjoy working beside people who celebrate each other's achievements. You’ll also do meaningful work, build great relationships, and help shape Victoria's energy future.

SEC offer flexible working options designed to support individual circumstances. To find more about our purpose and what it’s like to work at SEC, visit LinkedIn (linkedin.com/company/secvictoria) or their website (secvictoria.com.au).

How to apply
We strongly encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people. We are also deeply committed to building an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity and people with disability, people from the LGBTIQ community, and people from culturally diverse backgrounds. SEC strives to create a respectful and collaborative workplace culture that allows all employees to thrive.

For further information and to explore this opportunity further please contact SECRecruitment@davidsonwp.com

Please click the ‘Apply Now’ button. As part of the application process, you will need to provide a copy of your resume and/ or a cover letter (optional) addressing how your skills, knowledge and experience will be relevant to this role. Note: Applicants must be an Australian citizen, permanent resident or hold a valid work permit to be eligible to apply.

Other important information:

  • You must be an Australian citizen, permanent resident or hold a valid work permit to be eligible to apply.

job.title: SAP OPIM Functional Consultant
job.description:
About the Company

Davidson Technology are working with a State Government Department to secure an experienced SAP OPIM Functional Consultant to work as part of a specialist Future State project.


About the Role

As an SAP S/4HANA Operational Procurement and Inventory Management (OPIM) Functional Consultant, you will play a key role in the Central Pharmacy Future State Project, supporting the delivery of a new modern Central Pharmacy facility and fit-for-purpose ERP and warehouse management environment for the department. You will assess the existing S/4HANA landscape and design, configure and implement pragmatic Materials Management solutions covering operational procurement, inventory replenishment, inventory control and reverse logistics, ensuring alignment with SAP best practice and the future Central Pharmacy operating model. You will design master data structures and WRICEF objects and ensure seamless integration across EWM, SD, FI/CO, BTP and relevant external systems, working closely with the S/4HANA Solution Architect and key business and technical stakeholders. You will produce detailed functional designs, process flows, configuration specifications, data standards and test documentation, while supporting unit, integration, UAT, performance and other testing activities. You will also contribute to cutover and production deployment, change management, knowledge transfer and capability uplift, and provide specialist troubleshooting during hypercare and stabilisation, ensuring the solution is scalable, secure, compliant and successfully transitioned into ongoing operations.


About You

To be successful in this role, you’ll bring a minimum of five years’ hands-on experience designing and implementing original embedded S/4HANA Materials Management solutions across greenfield implementations and/or complex live production environments. You will demonstrate the ability to create bespoke, fit-for-purpose OPIM solutions rather than relying on predefined templates, with strong capability across end-to-end solution design, configuration, WRICEF development and fit-gap analysis. You will be skilled at translating complex business requirements into scalable SAP solutions aligned with best practice, supported by strong analytical and problem-solving capability and a deep understanding of integration across EWM, SD, FI, BTP and external systems. You will have demonstrated experience delivering across the complete SAP lifecycle, including design, build, testing, cutover, deployment, hypercare and post-go-live stabilisation, combined with strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills across both technical and business audiences. SAP S/4HANA Materials Management certification and additional certifications across areas such as MM, SD or EWM will be highly regarded, as will previous experience delivering SAP solutions within healthcare, pharmaceutical or similarly complex regulated environments.


The Benefits

You will be offered a 15-month contract on an excellent hourly rate and the ability to negotiate a flexible working arrangement for the duration of the assignment as well as the potential for further extensions.


Please apply with current resume in Microsoft Word format only (.doc or .docx). Want to know more about Davidson? Visit us at www.davidsonwp.com

job.title: HR Advisor | Workforce & People
job.description:
HR Advisor | Workforce & People

Katherine West Health Board | Katherine, NT
$94,907 – $116,569 + 12% super | Salary packaging | Relocation support

Make your next HR role mean something.

Are you an experienced HR Advisor looking for broader exposure, greater autonomy and the opportunity to work somewhere your contribution genuinely matters?

Davidson is proud to partner with Katherine West Health Board (KWHB), an Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Organisation providing primary healthcare and health-related programs to Aboriginal communities across approximately 162,000km² of the remote Katherine West region.

KWHB has experienced significant organisational growth and is continuing to strengthen its Human Resources function to support its expanding workforce.

We're now seeking an experienced HR Advisor to join the team in Katherine.

Internally titled Workforce Coordinator, this is a broad, hands-on HR advisory role working closely with the Senior Manager Human Resources and supporting managers and employees across the organisation.

If you enjoy variety, like being close to the action and want the opportunity to develop across the breadth of HR rather than being confined to one specialist area, this could be a fantastic next move.

The opportunity

You'll become a trusted member of a growing HR team, providing practical advice and support across the employee lifecycle.

No two days are likely to look exactly the same.

You'll support managers with day-to-day HR matters, prepare employment documentation, oversee workforce compliance, contribute to HR reporting and process improvement, and help ensure employees joining KWHB have a consistent and culturally appropriate experience.

You'll also have exposure to workplace reviews and investigations, workforce planning and broader organisational improvement initiatives.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Providing practical HR advice and support to managers and employees
  • Interpreting and applying HR policies, procedures, employment legislation and relevant industrial instruments
  • Preparing contracts, variations, secondments and other employment documentation
  • Supporting recruitment, onboarding, induction and offboarding
  • Monitoring licences, registrations, checks, certifications and other workforce compliance requirements
  • Supporting remuneration changes, pay progression, allowances and contractual changes
  • Maintaining accurate employee records and HR information systems
  • Coordinating workforce logistics including travel, accommodation and remote workforce requirements
  • Preparing workforce reporting and identifying trends, risks and opportunities
  • Contributing to HR policy, procedure and process improvement
  • Supporting workplace reviews and investigations as required
  • Contributing to culturally appropriate induction, orientation and workforce development activities.

The position also provides an opportunity to support and mentor less experienced HR and administrative team members as the function continues to evolve.

About you

We're looking for an experienced HR generalist who is comfortable providing practical advice and doesn't need every answer handed to them.

You don't need to be the finished product or an ER/IR specialist. You do, however, need enough HR experience and judgement to work through an issue, interpret the relevant policy or legislation, provide sensible advice and recognise when something needs to be escalated.

You'll ideally bring:

  • Experience at HR Advisor, People & Culture Advisor, Senior HR Coordinator or similar level
  • Practical experience providing HR advice and support to managers
  • Sound knowledge of HR policies, procedures and relevant employment legislation
  • Experience across employment documentation and employee lifecycle processes
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Confidence managing multiple priorities and working autonomously
  • Strong administration, systems and attention to detail
  • Sound judgement, discretion and professionalism
  • A practical, solutions-focused approach
  • The ability to build trusted relationships across a diverse and geographically dispersed workforce.

Experience in health, community services, government, not-for-profit or an Aboriginal Community Controlled Organisation would be highly regarded, but isn't essential.

A qualification in Human Resources, Business or a related discipline is desirable rather than mandatory, with equivalent relevant experience also considered.

Working with Katherine West Health Board

This role is about more than providing HR advice from behind a desk.

KWHB supports employees across Katherine and remote Aboriginal communities throughout the Katherine West region. You'll work with people from diverse professional, cultural and community backgrounds and will need to approach those relationships with respect, curiosity and cultural humility.

KWHB is committed to the recruitment, retention and development of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander employees and to creating culturally safe workplaces where people can develop meaningful careers.

You'll occasionally travel to remote communities by road and/or light aircraft as part of the role.

What's on offer?

  • $94,907 – $116,569 + 12% super, negotiable based on relevant skills and experience
  • 6 weeks annual leave + 18% leave loading
  • 2 weeks personal leave
  • Annual CPI increases
  • Salary packaging up to $15,900 per FBT year
  • Meal & Entertainment Card up to $2,650
  • Remote Area Benefits
  • Novated leasing
  • Relocation assistance up to $3,000
  • 6–8 weeks accommodation support on relocation
  • Travel allowance for work-related travel
  • Mobile phone allowance
  • Flexible working arrangements
  • Generous professional development support
  • Strong internal career pathways
  • The opportunity to build a career within a respected Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Organisation.

Before you apply

This is a full-time permanent role based in Katherine, Northern Territory.

The successful candidate will need:

  • A current NT Driver's Licence or the ability to obtain one
  • A current NT Working with Children Clearance (Ochre Card) or ability to obtain
  • A current Criminal History Check or ability to obtain
  • COVID-19 immunisation – minimum one dose
  • High-level computer skills including Microsoft Office and HR information systems
  • The ability and willingness to travel to remote locations by road and/or light aircraft
  • A demonstrated understanding of Aboriginal cultural values and commitment to the advancement and self-determination of Aboriginal communities.

KWHB is also open to considering suitably experienced candidates already living in Australia on a visa, subject to assessment of individual visa conditions and work rights.

Candidates across Australia and New Zealand who are genuinely prepared to relocate to Katherine are encouraged to apply.

Interested?

If you're an HR Advisor looking for an opportunity that offers breadth, autonomy, purpose and the chance to make a meaningful contribution within a growing organisation, we'd love to hear from you.

To apply - Please note:

Due to the quick turnaround for this opportunity and anticipated application volumes, please submit your application directly through the advertised application link rather than emailing your resume to the consultant - This will ensure your application is captured promptly as part of the recruitment process.

Please apply with current resume in Microsoft Word format only (.doc or .docx) through the application portal. If you would like to have a confidential discussion, please contact Taylah Gurney. Want to know more about Davidson? Visit us at www.davidsonwp.com

Davidson acknowledges the Traditional Custodians of the lands on which we work and live. We are also committed to equal opportunity and strive to promote diversity, inclusion, belonging, flexibility, and accessibility in all that we do.

Should you require assistance in your interactions with us or through a recruitment process, please let us know so we can provide adjustments for you.

job.title: Environment Coordinator
job.description:
JOB OVERVIEW:

We are seeking an experienced Environment Coordinator to join a major technology program in Melbourne, supporting the management and coordination of non-production Development and Test environments across multiple projects.

The role will focus on ensuring environments are available, stable, correctly configured and ready for development, integration and regression testing. You will work closely with project teams, testing teams, infrastructure and architecture stakeholders, release teams and support teams to coordinate environment requirements and resolve environment-related issues.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Manage and coordinate non-production Development and Test environments across assigned projects.
  • Coordinate environment requirements and manage environment bookings using Plutora.
  • Ensure environments are available, configured and ready for integration and regression testing.
  • Coordinate code deployments, database refreshes and environment preparation for monthly enterprise releases.
  • Work closely with project, development, testing, infrastructure, architecture and release teams to manage environment dependencies.
  • Provide technical guidance on environment configuration, testing, implementation and troubleshooting.
  • Coordinate database refresh activities and document data flows across integrated non-production environments.
  • Support the transformation of manual and high-risk environment processes into a more streamlined, automated and cloud-based ecosystem.
  • Manage environment-related defects and incidents through to resolution, escalating where required.
  • Troubleshoot server and application environment issues and coordinate with relevant support teams to identify owners and drive resolution.
  • Support applications including Acurity, Objective, Kofax and Sitecore across environment incidents, problems and outages.
  • Coordinate with Infrastructure and Integration Solution Architects on network and integration connectivity requirements.
  • Coordinate with Release teams on project requirements for out-of-cycle and enterprise releases.
  • Support project Hypercare following Go-Live, including retrofitting production code to lower environments where required.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement of environment management processes and practices.

What We're Looking For:

  • Strong hands-on experience managing non-production environments, particularly Development, Test and/or UAT environments.
  • Demonstrated experience coordinating environment availability, configuration, deployments, data refreshes and connectivity across multiple teams.
  • Practical Plutora experience is highly desirable and is a key requirement for this role.
  • Experience working with release, testing, development and project teams in a complex technology environment.
  • Strong troubleshooting and environment incident/defect management skills.
  • Experience with tools such as ServiceNow and JIRA is advantageous.
  • Financial services experience is preferred; superannuation industry experience would be beneficial but is not essential.
  • Strong stakeholder coordination and communication skills.
  • Ability to work effectively in a shared-responsibility environment and manage multiple competing environment requirements.

Contract Details:

  • Location: Melbourne
  • Work Arrangement: Hybrid – generally 3 days in the office
  • Start Date: 16 November 2026
  • Initial Contract: Until 4 January 2027
  • Extension: Potential to continue beyond the initial end date, with the current expectation potentially extending into the second week of January, subject to project requirements.



Please apply with current resume in Microsoft Word format only (.doc or .docx). If you would like to have a confidential discussion, please contact Bidisha Swayamprava on Bidisha.Swayamprava@davidsonwp.com, quoting reference JN -082026-44119. Want to know more about Davidson? Visit us at www.davidsonwp.com

job.title: Payroll Data Compliance Officer
job.description:
About the Company

Our client is a large, well-established organisation with operations across Australia and New Zealand. With the scale and structure of a major corporate environment, they offer excellent employee benefits, established systems and processes, and genuine opportunities for internal career progression.

Due to an internal promotion, an opportunity has become available for a Payroll Audit & Compliance Officer to join their experienced payroll function based in Milton.


About the Role

This is a great opportunity for someone with payroll experience who enjoys the auditing, compliance and investigative side of payroll rather than simply processing pay runs. Working alongside a team of payroll professionals, you will play an important quality-control role between HR and Payroll. Your focus will be reviewing and validating employee information before it flows through for payroll processing, ensuring changes are accurate, appropriately authorised and compliant.

Importantly, this role does not process payroll. Instead, you will audit employee master data, identify discrepancies and work closely with HR to resolve issues before they have an impact on employees' pay.

The role will include:

  • Reviewing and validating new employee set-ups, including positions, employment conditions and pay rates
  • Auditing employee changes before they are released to Payroll
  • Reviewing permanent and temporary remuneration increases
  • Checking higher duties and acting arrangements
  • Validating position changes, transfers and cost centre changes
  • Ensuring effective dates, rates and supporting information are correct
  • Identifying errors, missing information and inconsistencies in employee data
  • Investigating unusual transactions and determining what needs to be corrected
  • Maintaining accurate employee master data and appropriate audit trails
  • Working closely with HR to resolve incorrect or incomplete information
  • Liaising with Payroll to ensure validated information is available within payroll deadlines
  • Identifying recurring data-quality issues and supporting improvements to processes and controls

The Benefits

  • $90,000–$95,000 plus superannuation
  • 14% employer superannuation
  • Work from home every Tuesday
  • Flexible start times from 7:30am
  • 25% annual leave loading, paid each December
  • Annual remuneration reviews each January
  • TOIL accrual
  • Genuine internal career opportunities, with this position becoming available due to an internal promotion

About You

You will ideally come from a payroll background and have a strong understanding of employee master data and the information required to ensure employees are paid correctly. You may be an experienced Payroll Officer looking to move away from high-volume processing into a role focused more heavily on audit, compliance, controls and data integrity.

You will have excellent attention to detail and be naturally inclined to question information that doesn't look right, rather than simply processing what has been provided. You will also be comfortable following up with HR and other stakeholders when information is incomplete or incorrect.

The successful candidate will be required to complete pre-employment screening, including a criminal history check and drug and alcohol testing.


Please apply with your current resume in Microsoft Word format only (.doc or .docx). If you would like to have a confidential discussion, please contact Britt Molony on +61 0417737307, quoting reference JN -082026-44106. Want to know more about Davidson? Visit us at www.davidsonwp.com

job.title: Chief Marketing Officer
job.description:
• Global CMO growth mandate
  • Proven Founding Team
  • Join the next Agentic AI breakout business

We are partnering with a highly experienced technology founding team to appoint the Chief Marketing Officer for a new agentic AI software venture currently operating in stealth.

This is not a conventional startup. The business is being spun out of a successful, fast-growth technology company by a seasoned team of founders and operators who have built and scaled businesses before. With an initial team and technology already in place, a global go-to-market strategy and plans for external venture funding, the foundations are there to move quickly.

The company is building in one of the most important emerging areas of enterprise AI: enabling organisations to adopt and scale autonomous AI agents safely and responsibly. It is an early and rapidly developing category with significant global potential.

The opportunity is to join at the beginning, inherit an initial marketing team of approximately four and build the marketing engine from the ground up.

We are looking for a commercial, high-agency CMO who has lived through genuine startup or scale-up growth. Someone who knows what it takes to turn an emerging technology business into a significant international company.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You will own the marketing agenda, establish the growth engine and help take the business into multiple international markets from day one. Success will be measured commercially through pipeline, customer acquisition, qualified opportunities, conversion and revenue growth.

You are likely to have:

  • Built or scaled marketing inside a high-growth technology, SaaS or software business
  • Been part of a company that achieved meaningful commercial scale
  • Experience taking products into multiple international markets
  • Strong demand-generation and pipeline credentials
  • A highly analytical and metrics-driven approach
  • Genuine fluency with AI, automation, CRM and modern marketing technology
  • The ability to use technology and automation to create leverage rather than simply adding headcount
  • The confidence to market sophisticated products to technical and senior enterprise audiences
  • The energy and ambition to operate at genuine startup speed

Just as importantly, we are looking for someone who doesn't wait to be told what to do.

You will work alongside experienced, fast-moving founders who want an executive capable of seeing the opportunity, setting the agenda and driving it - someone who likes being one or two steps ahead while remaining prepared to get into the detail and execute personally.

The business will operate internationally from inception, initially across Australia, Asia and the Middle East. The role can be based in Melbourne or Sydney, with Melbourne preferred.

For the right person, this is a rare opportunity to join a seasoned technology team at inception, build in one of the most exciting areas of AI, and participate meaningfully in the value created as the business scales.

The company remains confidential while operating in stealth. Further details will be shared with suitably qualified candidates through the process.

To apply, please click ‘apply now’ and upload your CV and Cover Letter. For a confidential discussion, please contact Luke Henningsen on +61 403 468 888 / Luke.Henningsen@davidsonwp.com

job.title: Chief Operating Officer, Health and Branch Network – GMHBA
job.description:
• Lead a diverse network of health services and private health insurance branches
  • Drive growth, operational performance and an exceptional customer experience
  • Join the Executive Management Team – Geelong location

GMHBA is seeking an accomplished executive to lead its Health and Branch Network and deliver the next phase of its health services strategy. Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer and working as a key member of the Executive Management Team, the Chief Operating Officer – Health and Branch Network will have strategic and operational responsibility for a diverse portfolio spanning private health insurance branches, general practice, dental, physiotherapy, eyecare and integrated health hubs.

Leading six direct reports and approximately 140 employees, this executive will provide clear direction across a complex, customer-facing network. The mandate is to improve commercial performance, strengthen clinical and operational governance, enhance customer and patient experiences, and build an engaged, accountable and high-performing workforce.

With full profit and loss accountability, you will lead GMHBA’s Health and Branch Network, driving sustainable growth, operational performance and exceptional member and patient experiences. You will optimise the operating model, advance the integration of health and insurance services, and maintain strong clinical governance, risk and compliance standards. As a member of the Executive Management Team, you will help shape GMHBA’s broader strategy and investment priorities while building an engaged, collaborative and high-performing leadership culture across the network.

You are a commercially astute and values-led executive with significant experience leading complex, multi-site operations. You combine strategic perspective with operational discipline and are equally comfortable shaping long-term direction, improving business performance and engaging frontline teams. You will bring:

  • At least 10 years’ experience in senior leadership roles, ideally reporting to a CEO or divisional executive
  • Experience leading a network of healthcare providers and/or retail financial services locations
  • A demonstrated record of executing commercial turnaround, growth or performance-improvement strategies
  • Strong commercial acumen and experience managing a substantial profit and loss portfolio
  • A sound understanding of the primary care environment and policy context and/or financial services
  • Experience leading frontline operations, customer service delivery and network expansion
  • The ability to influence and engage diverse stakeholders at Board, executive and operational levels
  • A proven ability to build capable leadership teams and create an accountable, inclusive and high-performance culture
  • A relevant tertiary qualification in health, commerce, business or management; an MBA will be highly regarded

This is a significant executive appointment for a leader motivated by the opportunity to bring together commercial performance, healthcare delivery and customer value.

To view the Success Profile for this opportunity, please copy and paste the following link into your browser: https://tinyurl.com/4htpjzeu

job.title: Interim WHS Consultant – Governance & Compliance
job.description:
Our client is a large, statewide public vocational education and training provider seeking an experienced WHS Consultant to provide practical governance, compliance and risk support on an interim basis.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced WHS, governance, risk or compliance consultant who can quickly understand a complex environment, work from existing frameworks and get important work moving.

About the opportunity
This is not a traditional frontline WHS advisory role, nor is it a greenfield assignment requiring a new framework to be created from scratch.

The organisation already has an existing WHS and safety management framework, templates and governance materials. The focus of this assignment will be to put the practical structure and delivery around that framework, including:

  • Reviewing existing WHS policies, processes, governance documentation and terms of reference
  • Identifying key gaps, priorities and opportunities for improvement
  • Strengthening practical WHS governance arrangements
  • Engaging with the WHS Committee, WHS Network and key stakeholders
  • Consulting on and implementing agreed governance processes
  • Working alongside an existing safety resource to align the safety management and governance frameworks
  • Providing clear updates to senior stakeholders
  • Identifying and escalating risk exposure early and appropriately
  • Preparing clear documentation and handover material for the permanent appointee

About the organisation
The organisation is a large, statewide public vocational education and training provider with a diverse network of campuses, trade training facilities, workshops, learning environments and corporate services.

It operates across a complex and highly governed environment, supporting a broad workforce and a wide range of students, industries and communities throughout Queensland.

About you
You will be an experienced consultant or practitioner with strong capability across WHS governance, compliance, risk or safety management.

You will ideally bring:

  • Experience working across WHS governance, compliance, risk or safety management
  • Strong policy, process and governance framework experience
  • Experience developing or reviewing terms of reference and committee structures
  • Confidence working with senior leaders, executives, boards or board subcommittees
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and consultation skills
  • The ability to translate frameworks and obligations into practical actions
  • Clear written and verbal communication
  • A self-directed, pragmatic and outcomes-focused approach
  • Experience working in government, education, health, resources, mining or another complex organisation

Exposure to child safety legislative changes would be highly regarded but is not essential.

A relevant qualification in WHS, risk, governance, compliance, law, public administration or a related discipline is desirable. A Blue Card is not required for the role.

Working arrangements:

job.title: APS6 Senior Media Officer
job.description:
About the Company

The Australian Digital Health Agency is driving a healthier future for Australians through connected healthcare.

Responsible for national digital health services and systems, the Agency is focused on improving health outcomes through the effective use of data and technology. Its work supports patients, consumers and healthcare professionals by helping make health information more accessible, progressive and secure.

With a strong focus on engagement, innovation, clinical quality and safety, the Agency works collaboratively to accelerate the adoption and use of innovative digital services and technologies across Australia.

The Corporate Services Division brings together high-quality enabling services to ensure they are coordinated, effective and mutually reinforcing.


About the Role

As Senior Media Officer (APS6), you will join a pool of marketing and communications professionals providing flexible, responsive support across Agency work plan projects.

You will develop and implement strategic media and communications materials that support Agency activities, products and strategic narratives. Working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment, you will help ensure communications are accurate, consistent and aligned with strategic objectives and stakeholder needs.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Developing, implementing and evaluating media and communications strategies, plans and campaigns
  • Crafting compelling narratives and positive media stories
  • Providing expert media advice to senior executives, spokespeople, subject matter experts and stakeholders
  • Managing complex and sensitive media issues and responding professionally to media enquiries
  • Producing strategic content for internal and external audiences and channels
  • Monitoring, analysing and reporting on media performance, trends and engagement
  • Managing media and communications projects from inception through to delivery
  • Building productive relationships across government, media, industry and community stakeholders
  • Identifying communications risks and opportunities and contributing to effective issues management
  • Working collaboratively across the Agency to deliver high-quality communications outcomes.

You will exercise a high degree of independence, initiative and judgement, while managing competing priorities and delivering quality work in an environment where requirements can change quickly.

The position can be based in Brisbane, Canberra or Sydney. It is a five-day-per-week role with a rotation of weekend on-call duties, with an estimated 37.5-hour working week. Some remote work may be considered once established, and travel and work outside normal business hours may be required.


About You

You are an experienced media and communications professional who understands the contemporary media landscape and can confidently operate in a complex, high-profile environment.

  • A degree in Journalism, Media and Communications, Marketing or another relevant field
  • A minimum of five years’ experience in media relations, journalism or external communications
  • Demonstrated experience developing and executing effective media and communications strategies
  • Strong writing and storytelling skills, with the ability to develop clear and compelling narratives
  • A detailed understanding of the current media landscape
  • Experience managing competing priorities and delivering effectively under pressure
  • Outstanding organisational, interpersonal and communication skills
  • Strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to influence and build productive relationships
  • The ability to analyse media engagement and performance and translate insights into recommendations
  • Sound judgement, initiative and discretion when managing complex or sensitive matters
  • A collaborative approach combined with the ability to self-manage and progress work independently.

Australian Citizenship is a condition of eligibility. You must also be able to obtain and maintain a Baseline security clearance, with the capacity to obtain a higher clearance if required, and obtain and maintain a national police check.


The Benefits

This opportunity provides the chance to contribute to work with national significance while building your career within a progressive Australian Government agency.

You will benefit from:

  • Meaningful work supporting Australia’s digital health agenda
  • Exposure to diverse, high-profile media and communications matters
  • The opportunity to advise senior leaders and work with stakeholders across government, media, industry and the community
  • A collaborative environment that values innovation, accountability, transparency, respect and working together
  • Flexible working arrangements designed to support effective hybrid teams
  • Opportunities to contribute to strategic initiatives and the Agency’s reputation as a leader in digital health innovation.

If you are an accomplished media professional who thrives in a changing environment and wants to use your expertise to support better health outcomes for Australians, this is an opportunity to make a meaningful contribution.


How to Apply

Please apply with current resume in Microsoft Word format only (.doc or .docx). If you would like to have a confidential discussion, please contact Natalee Thorpe (Natalee.thorpe@davidsonwp.com), quoting reference JN -082026-44123.
