job.title: Agile Delivery Manager
job.description:
Agile Delivery Manager

Do you thrive on transforming how technology teams deliver, bringing structure to complex environments and embedding practical Agile ways of working? If you're a hands-on delivery leader who can create clarity, challenge existing practices and drive greater accountability and delivery performance, we'd love to hear from you.

About the Role

Our client, a well-established national organisation, is seeking an experienced Agile Delivery Manager to play a key role within a major enterprise technology transformation centred around the implementation of Microsoft Dynamics 365.

Working alongside an external Systems Integrator responsible for the core D365 implementation, you'll take ownership of the internal technology delivery required to successfully integrate the new platform into the broader organisation. This includes coordinating work across integration, data, business requirements and readiness, while managing dependencies between internal technology teams, the SI and business stakeholders.

A key focus will be strengthening how the internal technology team delivers. You'll establish practical Agile delivery disciplines, improve planning and workflow through Scrum and Kanban practices, create greater visibility through Azure DevOps and ensure work has clear ownership, requirements and definitions of done.

This isn't a traditional Project Manager or Scrum Master role. We're looking for a hands-on delivery leader who can combine Agile delivery expertise with strong technical understanding and stakeholder influence. You'll need to quickly understand what is happening across multiple workstreams, challenge where required and establish the structure, standards and accountability needed to drive delivery forward.

Your responsibilities will include but not be limited to:

· Take ownership of delivery planning across internal technology workstreams, creating a clear view of scope, priorities, milestones, dependencies and responsibilities.
· Create greater visibility of work and delivery progress through effective use of Azure DevOps and associated delivery tooling.
· Establish clear expectations around how work is defined, documented, tracked and progressed, including agreed definitions of what "done" looks like.
· Ensure technical designs, requirements, decisions and approvals are appropriately documented and managed throughout delivery.
· Work closely with the Systems Integrator, internal technology teams and business stakeholders to clarify ownership and ensure delivery activities remain aligned.
· Improve planning practices to ensure delivery commitments are supported by clearly understood scope, capacity, dependencies and technical requirements.
· Proactively identify delivery risks, gaps, dependencies and blockers and drive these through to resolution.
· Challenge assumptions and delivery updates where required, ensuring teams remain accountable for agreed standards, actions and outcomes.
· Bring greater consistency, transparency and predictability to technology delivery across the broader transformation.

Skills and experience – To be successful in this role, you will bring:

· Proven experience as a Delivery Manager, Agile Delivery Lead or similar within complex enterprise technology environments.
· Demonstrated experience establishing or improving delivery disciplines, standards and ways of working across technology teams.
· Experience managing delivery across areas such as ERP, enterprise applications, integration, data and cloud technologies.
· Strong technical understanding, with the ability to interrogate delivery updates, ask the right questions and identify potential risks or gaps.
· Strong planning and delivery management capabilities, with experience creating visibility across multiple interconnected workstreams.
· Exceptional stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the confidence to challenge existing practices and hold teams accountable for agreed outcomes.
· Experience working within large or sophisticated enterprise environments such as financial services, superannuation, energy, utilities or similar industries will be highly regarded.

This is an outstanding opportunity to play a key role within a major enterprise transformation and have a genuine impact on how technology delivery is managed across the organisation.

You'll be joining a close-knit technology team where you'll have the opportunity to introduce stronger delivery practices, create greater clarity and accountability, and establish ways of working that support both the immediate transformation and longer-term technology capability.

This is an initial 9-month fixed-term opportunity based in the Western Suburbs, with a minimum of three days onsite per week and a preference for four. The role offers a competitive package, with the opportunity to make a significant impact during a critical stage of the organisation’s technology transformation.

How to Apply

If this opportunity aligns with your experience and career aspirations, please submit your current CV in Microsoft Word format (.doc or .docx)

For a confidential discussion, please contact Cameron Smith at cameron.smith@davidsonwp.com

To learn more about Davidson, visit www.davidsonwp.com

job.title: SAP ABAP Developer x 3
job.description:
About the Company

Davidson Technology are working with a State Government Department to secure multiple SAP ABAP Developers to work as part of a specialist Future State project. The contracts range in length from 11-months to 14-0months located either in Brisbane or Richlands.


About the Role

As an SAP ABAP Developer, you will work as part of a specialist delivery team supporting the department’s Central Pharmacy Future State (CPFS) Project, helping deliver a modern enterprise platform that supports WMS, ERP and the future operating model of the new Central Pharmacy facility. You will assess and enhance the existing SAP S/4HANA environment, translating complex functional and business requirements into scalable, maintainable and upgrade-safe technical solutions aligned with SAP clean-core principles. You will design and develop in-app, developer and side-by-side extensions using technologies including ABAP RAP, CDS Views, released APIs, SAP BTP, CAP, SAP Fiori and SAPUI5, while developing OData services and HANA data models and integrating SAP and non-SAP systems through BTP Integration Suite, Extension Suite and Identity Services. Working closely with functional consultants, business stakeholders and technical teams, you will deliver assigned development milestones, undertake unit testing, manage changes across development, test and production environments, troubleshoot post-implementation issues and conduct code and specification reviews to ensure performance, security and quality standards are maintained. You will also proactively identify opportunities to improve application performance, user experience and development practices, maintain comprehensive technical documentation, and transfer knowledge to departmental employees to build sustainable internal SAP capability.


About You

To be successful in this role, you’ll ideally bring 7–10 years of experience contributing to complex, large-scale SAP implementations, with strong SAP S/4HANA development expertise and comprehensive knowledge of SAP BTP services and architecture. You will demonstrate hands-on development capability across ABAP, RAP Business Objects, BADI, BAPI, IDOC, SAP Fiori configuration and extensions, SAPUI5, SAP Web IDE, JavaScript, HTML5, Adobe Forms and BTP Forms by Adobe Services, together with experience supporting RF mobile data entry solutions. You will possess strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to assess complex supply chain requirements, develop and communicate technical solution options, and translate these into fit-for-purpose system and process improvements supported by high-quality technical specifications. You will have a sound understanding of contemporary integration approaches and service-oriented architecture, while bringing a collaborative approach to knowledge sharing and developing team capability. Experience within complex government, healthcare or pharmaceutical environments and SAP development exposure across FI/CO, MM, SD and particularly Extended Warehouse Management (EWM) will be highly regarded, alongside SAP S/4HANA and BTP certifications.


The Benefits

You will be offered a contract up to 14-month on an excellent hourly rate and the ability to work from either the Brisbane or Richland offices.

Please apply with current resume in Microsoft Word format only (.doc or .docx). Want to know more about Davidson? Visit us at www.davidsonwp.com

job.title: HL7 Data Architect
job.description:
About the Company

Davidson Technology are working with a leading Federal Government Agency to secure an experienced HL7 FHIR Data Architect responsible for the design and development of clinical information products, such as HL7 FHIR Implementation Guides, and services that drive national health data interoperability improvements and other strategic priorities.


About the Role

As an HL7 Data Architect, you will lead the design and development of clinical information products and services that support national health data interoperability, including HL7 FHIR Implementation Guides and interoperable health record data models. You will apply specialist expertise across conceptual, information and implementation modelling to translate complex clinical and stakeholder requirements into high-quality, implementable standards and solutions. Working with a high degree of independence, you will provide authoritative technical advice, anticipate and resolve complex issues, undertake quality assurance and contribute to strategic planning, innovation and continuous improvement initiatives. You will provide technical leadership and mentoring to build capability across the team, support the prioritisation and delivery of work, and ensure outputs meet relevant standards, regulations and best-practice principles. A key focus will be engaging collaboratively with national and international standards bodies, Australian jurisdictions, industry and the broader health informatics community to develop and improve interoperability standards, while maintaining strong stakeholder networks and communicating complex clinical informatics concepts, products and outcomes to both technical and non-technical audiences.


About You

To be successful in this role, you will bring strong hands-on experience designing and developing solutions using HL7 FHIR, with a detailed understanding of FHIR standards and associated validation and expression languages such as FHIRPath. You will have demonstrated expertise developing information models, FHIR profiles and Implementation Guides, including practical experience with HL7 authoring and publishing technologies such as the FHIR Publisher to produce standards-compliant, implementable clinical information products. You will also demonstrate sound knowledge of contemporary software source code management and version control practices, enabling effective collaboration, traceability, quality assurance and controlled development of FHIR artefacts. Your combination of technical FHIR expertise, structured development practices and understanding of health interoperability standards will enable you to contribute effectively to complex national digital health initiatives, with formal HL7 FHIR certification considered highly desirable.

This role requires Australian Citizenship and the ability to obtain and maintain a Baseline security clearance (with potential for higher clearance if required) and a national police check.


The Benefits

You will be offered an excellent daily rate on a 9-month contract in a hybrid working environment.

job.title: Senior Consultant - Business Advisory
job.description:
About Davidson

Davidson is one of Australia’s leading workplace performance companies. For over 30 years, we have partnered with public and private sector clients to enhance workplace performance.

Davidson Business Advisory delivers pragmatic, outcome-focused advice grounded in industry knowledge and consulting expertise. We work alongside clients to achieve measurable and sustainable impact across Strategy & Operations, Transformation Delivery and Talent & Leadership Advisory. Our experienced team combines practical insight with proven consulting methodologies to help organisations navigate transformation, strengthen performance and create sustainable outcomes.

About the Role

We are seeking a Senior Consultant to join our Business Advisory team, helping clients solve complex organisational challenges and enhance workplace performance.

Reporting to a Senior Partner, you will take ownership of consulting workstreams, combining financial and commercial analysis, structured problem-solving and stakeholder insight to deliver practical, measurable outcomes.

You will support and increasingly lead stakeholder interviews and workshops, engage directly with client stakeholders and translate complex information into clear, practical recommendations. As your capability develops, you will take on increasingly complex work and greater responsibility for day-to-day client relationships.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Manage defined consulting workstreams with increasing independence, maintaining quality, scope and agreed timeframes.
  • Undertake financial and operational analysis, research, data analysis and benchmarking to identify key value drivers and develop evidence-based recommendations.
  • Facilitate stakeholder interviews, workshops and discussions with executive, management and operational audiences.
  • Develop clear, compelling reports, presentations and other client deliverables tailored to the audience.
  • Build trusted client relationships through professionalism, responsiveness, sound judgement and genuine care.
  • Work collaboratively with Senior Partners and multidisciplinary project teams to deliver high-quality outcomes.
  • Contribute to proposals, client presentations and broader business development opportunities.
  • Identify opportunities to extend client value through additional advisory services where appropriate.
  • Contribute to thought leadership, research, consulting methodologies and intellectual property.
  • Share knowledge and provide guidance to Consultants and Graduates, helping strengthen capability across the team.
  • Bring curiosity and contemporary thinking to organisational and workplace challenges while maintaining commercial discipline in project delivery.

What We’re Looking For

You will bring experience from management consulting, business advisory or a comparable professional services environment, with strong financial analysis capability and demonstrated experience across transformation or strategy engagements.

You will ideally demonstrate:

  • Strong financial analysis skills, with the ability to analyse financial and operational data, identify key value drivers and translate findings into commercially sound recommendations.
  • Demonstrated experience in either transformation or strategy, with the ability to contribute to complex engagements and deliver practical, sustainable outcomes.
  • Experience delivering consulting engagements involving research, analysis, stakeholder engagement and workshop facilitation.
  • Strong critical-thinking and problem-solving capability, with the ability to structure complex problems and develop evidence-based recommendations.
  • Well-developed written and verbal communication skills, including high-quality reports, presentations and client documentation.
  • Confidence engaging and facilitating discussions with executive, management and operational stakeholders.
  • Strong commercial awareness and an understanding of scope, efficiency, quality and value in consulting delivery.
  • A relevant tertiary qualification in Business, Commerce, Human Resources, Psychology, Public Policy or a related discipline.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft PowerPoint, Excel, Word, and Canva highly regarded.

Experience across organisational transformation, strategy, workforce, leadership or operating model engagements would be highly regarded, as would postgraduate qualifications or relevant consulting, project management or change management certifications.

Above all, we are looking for someone who is curious about how organisations and people perform, takes pride in producing excellent work and wants to continue developing as a trusted adviser.

Why Join Davidson

At Davidson, we believe when people thrive, organisations thrive. You will be part of a collaborative, value-driven organisation putting people at the centre of its success. We offer the autonomy to make decisions, supported by access to senior leadership and a lean operating model that clears the path rather than clogs it.

  • A national brand with strong market presence and long-term client relationships.
  • A flexible, hybrid work environment.
  • A culture defined by purpose, excellence, care and opportunity.
  • Direct access to decision makers through a flat, agile structure.
  • Learning and development opportunities tailored to your career goals.
  • Recognition programs celebrating individual and team contributions.
  • Fun things we do include – high achievers' lunches, monthly celebration hours, values awards, steak & chips nights.

Ready to step into your next chapter?

If you are looking to build on your consulting experience, work directly with experienced leaders and help clients solve meaningful people and organisational challenges, we would welcome the opportunity to hear from you.

Apply today to join Davidson as our next Senior Consultant – Business Advisory.

job.title: Sharepoint Specialist (Collaboration Transition)
job.description:
About the Company

Davidson Technology are working with a large State Government Department to secure an experienced Sharepoint Specialist to support a Machinery of Government (MOG) M365 Collaboration transition.


About the Role

As a SharePoint Specialist (Collaboration Transition), you will play a key role in supporting the successful transition of SharePoint Online sites and collaboration content into the department’s Microsoft 365 environment as part of the Digital MarketPlace Machinery of Government project. You will work closely with business site owners, multiple departmental and inter department stakeholders and the internal technical resources to assess existing SharePoint sites, determine migration readiness and identify required remediation or configuration changes. You will apply hands-on SharePoint Online expertise across modern sites, pages, web parts, navigation, document libraries, lists, views, metadata, permissions and publishing functionality to prepare sites for transition and ensure they operate effectively in the target environment. You will support migration activities using ShareGate where appropriate, validate migrated sites from both technical and end-user perspectives, and troubleshoot issues relating to access, navigation, links, content and functionality. You will also identify unsupported, obsolete or customised SharePoint components, recommend appropriate treatment, document outstanding issues and support a smooth transition into business ownership and ongoing BAU support.


About You

To be successful in this role, you’ll bring a minimum of seven years’ experience working within large-scale enterprise environments, with strong hands-on expertise administering, configuring, remediating, troubleshooting and transitioning SharePoint Online solutions. You will have deep practical knowledge of modern SharePoint sites, including pages, web parts, navigation, document libraries, lists, views, permissions, metadata and Microsoft 365 group-connected sites, combined with demonstrated experience assessing and preparing existing sites for migration, identifying unsupported or custom components and implementing practical remediation solutions. You will work directly with business site owners and technical project teams to understand requirements, support migration activities and validate functionality following transition, ideally using ShareGate Migrate or comparable migration tooling. You will demonstrate strong troubleshooting capability across site usability, access, navigation, content and business functionality, while producing high-quality site assessments, transition runbooks, issue and exception registers, validation evidence and handover documentation. Your strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills will enable you to operate effectively across diverse business and technical audiences, with broader Microsoft 365 experience across Teams, OneDrive, Microsoft 365 Groups and Entra ID, and relevant Microsoft certifications, considered highly advantageous.


The Benefits

You will be offered a 6-month contract with the potential of a 3-month extension on an excellent hourly rate as well as a hybrid working environment.


Please apply with current resume in Microsoft Word format only (.doc or .docx). Want to know more about Davidson? Visit us at www.davidsonwp.com

job.title: Executive Director (Logan to Gold Coast Faster Rail)
job.description:
• Leading a major transport investment shaping South East Queensland’s rail future
  • Drive whole-of-program performance across complex, multidisciplinary delivery
  • Enable capacity, reliability and connectivity outcomes for South East Queensland

Transport and Main Roads (TMR)

Transport and Main Roads (TMR) is Queensland’s lead agency for integrated transport systems and infrastructure, responsible for planning, building, managing and maintaining one of Australia’s largest and most diverse transport networks. The department oversees more than 33,000 kilometres of state-controlled roads and coordinates public transport across South East Queensland, while also delivering major rail, road and active transport infrastructure programs. In addition, TMR leads policy, regulation and long-term transport planning for a rapidly growing state.

TMR plays a critical role in enabling economic growth, regional development and community connectivity across Queensland, from metropolitan centres to regional and remote communities. With a workforce of more than 8,500 people, the department brings together deep expertise across engineering, project delivery, planning, policy and customer services. It is at the forefront of delivering city-shaping, state-significant infrastructure aligned to population growth and the Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games. Driven by a commitment to safety, sustainability and innovation, TMR is focused on creating a transport system that is accessible, resilient and future ready.

The Opportunity

TMR is seeking an accomplished infrastructure executive to join the Rail Infrastructure Delivery Office (RIDO) as Executive Director, Logan and Gold Coast Faster Rail (LGCFR).

Valued at $5.75 billion, LGCFR is one of Queensland’s largest and most complex infrastructure investments. The program will increase rail capacity, reliability and connectivity across South East Queensland through major corridor upgrades, station improvements, level crossing removals and active transport infrastructure across approximately 20 kilometres between Kuraby and Beenleigh.

Reporting to the General Manager, RIDO, you will lead the delivery phase of the program, ensuring successful outcomes across time, cost and quality objectives while maintaining strong governance, commercial performance and stakeholder engagement. You will also be responsible for managing critical interfaces with major rail initiatives including Cross River Rail, ETCS Level 2, New Gold Coast Stations and the Queensland Train Manufacturing Program to ensure coordinated outcomes across the broader rail network.

The Role

As Executive Director, you will lead the end-to-end delivery of the LGCFR program, ensuring design and construction activities are effectively coordinated across multiple project packages. You will provide strategic oversight of commercial, financial, procurement and governance activities, while ensuring delivery partners, consultants and contractors remain aligned to program objectives. You will be accountable for program performance and will report on progress against time, cost and quality objectives, while ensuring that commercial strategies and negotiations deliver optimal value for the State.

You will provide strong leadership to multidisciplinary teams, consultants and contractors, fostering a collaborative and high-performing environment that enables successful delivery outcomes. You will also lead stakeholder engagement efforts, maintaining trusted and productive relationships with Queensland Rail, delivery partners, local councils and community stakeholders.

As the senior escalation point, you will manage complex engineering, contractual, financial and delivery issues, ensuring timely resolution and continuous improvement across the program. You will oversee the development of program plans, submissions and executive reporting, and provide expert advice to senior leaders and government stakeholders. This role also requires effective management of interfaces with other major rail initiatives ensuring alignment and integration across the broader network.

About You

You are a proven executive leader with extensive experience ideally delivering brownfield rail or major rail infrastructure in complex operational environments. You understand the challenges of delivering significant construction within and alongside an operating railway and the critical interfaces associated.

You have successfully led large multidisciplinary teams, major contractors and delivery partners and can make high-quality strategic and commercial decisions in complex environments.

You bring strong systems integration and technical assurance capability, together with the discipline to monitor whole-of-program performance and manage safety, commercial, technical and delivery risks.

An influential stakeholder leader, you can build trusted relationships across government, the rail operator and delivery partners, reconcile competing priorities and communicate complex issues clearly to senior executives and government stakeholders.

You lead with clarity, accountability and sound judgement and have the resilience and strategic perspective required to operate successfully in a highly scrutinised major infrastructure environment.

Relevant tertiary qualifications in engineering, law, commercial disciplines, project management or a related field will be highly regarded.

Why Join TMR

This is a once-in-a-generation opportunity to lead infrastructure that will have a lasting impact on Queensland. You will lead a $5.75 billion program spanning multiple delivery packages, technical systems and network interfaces, helping create the rail capacity and connectivity required to support one of Australia’s fastest-growing regions.

As a member of RIDO’s leadership team, you will also influence outcomes beyond an individual project, contributing to the integration of major rail investments and the future performance of South East Queensland’s transport network. TMR offers a purpose-driven, inclusive and collaborative environment where experienced leaders can make a tangible and enduring contribution to Queensland’s future.

job.title: Senior Data Analyst, Customer Insights
job.description:
About the Company

Davidson Technology are working with a large Queensland transportation organisation to secure a Senior Data Analyst, Customer Insights to join the team on an initial 4-month Fixed Term Contract with the potential to progress to a permanent employee.


About the Role

As a Senior Data Analyst, Customer Insights, you will lead the delivery of a comprehensive customer research and insights program that informs strategic decision-making and measures the effectiveness of key organisational priorities. You will design and execute qualitative and quantitative research across the organisation’s products, services and brands, undertaking detailed customer segmentation across users and non-users of specific services and developing ongoing brand and corporate reputation tracking. You’ll use customer journey mapping, demographic information, Go Card data and broader research to identify emerging transport trends, customer behaviours and opportunities to improve the end-to-end travel experience. Working closely with Corporate Strategy, TransLink, TMR and other stakeholders, you will translate complex data and research into actionable insights that influence customer-centric change, while developing new performance metrics across customer experience, brand, employees, products and services. You will also own and maintain a central Insights Register and partner with People & Culture to support the design, benchmarking, analysis and implementation of Employee Engagement survey outcomes.


About You

To be successful in this role, you will bring extensive experience delivering sophisticated market research and customer data analysis within large and complex organisations, with particular expertise across customer segmentation, brand and corporate reputation research, advertising testing and choice modelling. You will demonstrate the ability to analyse complex quantitative and qualitative information, identify meaningful trends and insights, translate research findings into practical business recommendations and influence stakeholders to drive customer-focused change. You will be highly proficient in Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint, data visualisation platforms such as Power BI and Tableau, and statistical analysis tools including SPSS or Q. Your strong written and verbal communication, interpersonal, influencing and negotiation skills will enable you to effectively communicate insights to both technical and non-technical audiences and build productive relationships across the organisation. You’ll also have substantial experience designing and implementing meaningful metrics across customer, brand, employee, product and service performance, alongside proven capability managing external research and service providers to ensure strategic research programs deliver high-quality, timely and commercially relevant outcomes.


The Benefits

job.title: Manager – Organisational Development
job.description:
Manager – Organisational Development

Logan, Queensland | TRP $173,182 – $185,502 p.a.

Lead an established team of OD and capability specialists within a large, diverse and complex organisation undergoing significant change.

We are partnering confidentially with a large and diverse organisation based in Logan to appoint an experienced Manager – Organisational Development.

This is a senior leadership opportunity for an accomplished Organisational Development practitioner who brings both deep OD expertise and demonstrated experience leading experienced specialist teams.

Operating within a large, multifaceted environment, you will lead an established team responsible for organisational development, leadership and capability, learning and talent pathways. Working closely with senior and executive leaders, you will translate organisational strategy into practical people and capability initiatives that can be successfully delivered and embedded across the organisation.

This is not simply an L&D, HR generalist or standalone change role.

We are looking for someone who has built their career within Organisational Development and can bring the professional credibility, leadership maturity and practical judgement required to lead an experienced team and operate effectively across a complex organisation.

The opportunity
Reporting to the General Manager of People & Culture, you will provide leadership and strategic direction across the organisation's OD and capability portfolio.

The organisation is continuing to evolve its people and organisational capability, and there is a genuine opportunity for the successful person to shape how OD supports the business into the future.

A key part of the role will be understanding the organisation's current level of maturity and ensuring initiatives are practical, appropriately paced and capable of being embedded.

You will be responsible for:

  • Leading and developing an established team of experienced OD, leadership, learning and capability specialists.
  • Providing subject matter expertise and strategic leadership across the Organisational Development portfolio.
  • Partnering with senior and executive leaders to identify organisational and workforce capability priorities.
  • Leading the design and implementation of enterprise-wide OD initiatives across areas including organisational capability, leadership, culture, talent, workforce development and organisational effectiveness.
  • Translating broader organisational strategy and transformation priorities into practical people initiatives and measurable outcomes.
  • Establishing clear priorities across a broad portfolio and ensuring the team remains focused on initiatives that deliver the greatest organisational value.
  • Building stakeholder ownership and successfully embedding initiatives across a large and diverse workforce.
  • Using evidence, data and organisational insights to inform priorities and measure impact.
  • Continuing to build the credibility, capability and impact of the OD function across the organisation.

About you
To be considered for this opportunity, you will need to demonstrate:

A relevant tertiary qualification in Organisational Development, Organisational Psychology/Psychology, Human Resources or a closely related discipline.

Substantial career experience in Organisational Development, with demonstrated breadth across enterprise OD rather than experience limited primarily to learning delivery, HR generalist work or standalone change management.

Demonstrated experience operating within a large, complex organisation, ideally supporting a workforce of 1,000+ employees across multiple functions, business units or operational environments.

Strong and recent people leadership experience, including responsibility for leading, developing and setting direction for experienced OD and/or capability specialists.

You will also bring:

  • Strong executive and senior stakeholder influencing capability.
  • Experience developing and implementing enterprise-wide OD, capability, leadership, culture or workforce initiatives.
  • The judgement to balance contemporary OD thinking with what an organisation is ready and able to successfully implement.
  • Demonstrated ability to prioritise competing initiatives and translate strategy into practical delivery.
  • Strong commercial and organisational acumen.
  • Confidence operating within environments with significant governance, stakeholder complexity and approval processes.
  • A collaborative but decisive leadership style, with the ability to challenge thinking, establish clear direction and hold people accountable for delivery.

Sector background is less important than organisational complexity. We are particularly interested in candidates who have operated within large, diverse and highly governed organisations, where successful delivery requires navigating multiple stakeholder groups, competing priorities and established governance and approval processes.

Why consider this opportunity?
This is an opportunity to take genuine ownership of an established Organisational Development function and influence how organisational capability continues to evolve.

You will work with experienced specialists, partner closely with senior leadership and have the opportunity to deliver work that has impact across a large and diverse organisation.

The role is based in Logan, Queensland and offers a Total Remuneration Package of $173,182 – $185,502 per annum.

Hybrid working arrangements of up to 3 days per fortnight are available however given the leadership nature of this position, candidates should be comfortable maintaining a regular onsite presence in Logan.

This appointment is being managed as a confidential search. Further information regarding the organisation and opportunity will be provided to suitably qualified candidates through the recruitment process.

job.title: L&D Advisor | $70.42–$73.57/hr + Super
job.description:
Contract until December 2026 | $70.42 per hour + super | Maroochydore and North Lakes sites

Are you an experienced L&D professional who enjoys taking a project, bringing the right people together and turning complex requirements into practical learning solutions?

We are partnering with a large, complex essential services organisation to recruit an experienced Learning & Development Advisor for an immediate-start labour hire contract through until the end of December, with potential for extension.

You'll join a small, collaborative L&D team with a substantial portfolio of work underway and a manager who genuinely encourages ownership, ideas and collective decision-making.

The opportunity
This isn't an L&D role centred predominantly around facilitation or leadership development.

Approximately 80% of the team's work supports safety and compliance learning, and you'll work across a combination of learning projects, accredited programs and BAU activity.

There are currently around 27 projects across the team, including the development of new safety and compliance eLearning modules, certificate programs, apprentice learning, learner resources and other L&D initiatives.

Depending on your experience and particular strengths, you may take ownership of several specific projects or work more broadly across the portfolio.

Your responsibilities may include:

  • Managing L&D projects from initial consultation through to delivery
  • Partnering with leaders and subject matter experts to understand learning and capability requirements
  • Gathering and interpreting information across policies, procedures, frameworks and data
  • Translating technical or compliance requirements into practical learning solutions
  • Supporting the development of new eLearning modules in partnership with an Instructional Designer
  • Keeping SMEs engaged throughout the development and review process
  • Supporting accredited training programs delivered through external RTOs
  • Working with leaders and HR Business Partners to identify and enrol appropriate program participants
  • Contributing to projects involving apprentice learning, learner guides, study assistance and other L&D initiatives
  • Managing competing priorities within an agile/project-based working environment.

About you
We're looking for an experienced L&D practitioner who is comfortable operating within a large and complex organisation and can confidently take ownership of work rather than waiting for every next step to be provided.

You'll ideally bring:

  • Solid Learning & Development experience gained within a corporate or similarly complex environment
  • Strong consultation and stakeholder engagement skills, particularly working with subject matter experts
  • Demonstrated experience managing L&D projects end to end
  • A sound understanding of learning design and adult learning principles
  • The ability to gather information, understand the bigger picture and join the dots across multiple requirements
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the confidence to come back with recommendations and a plan
  • Experience managing competing priorities and multiple stakeholders
  • Experience with LMS/HRIS learning environments and good general technology capability
  • Relevant qualifications in HR, Learning & Development, Training and Assessment or a related discipline.

Experience within an organisation supporting frontline, operational, technical, construction or similar workforces would be highly regarded, as would exposure to safety and compliance learning, but neither is essential.

We're interested in the depth and relevance of your experience, not simply the number of years you've worked in L&D.

Why consider this opportunity?
There is a lot happening in this team and that's part of what makes the opportunity interesting.

You'll join a genuinely collaborative group that enjoys the work they do, has strong relationships across the organisation and has recently adopted agile ways of working to better manage its project portfolio.

You'll be given clear projects and expectations, but also the space to bring your own L&D expertise, ideas and ways of solving problems.

The team is currently under-resourced, so your contribution will be meaningful from the outset.

Contract: ASAP start through to the end of December 2026, with potential for extension
Rate: Rates start at $70.42–$73.57 per hour + superannuation, depending on experience
Location: Maroochydore preferred, with North Brisbane also considered
Hybrid: Approximately 2–3 days per week in the office, with flexibility around start and finish times

job.title: Interim HR Administrator - Immediate start
job.description:
Short-term contract | Brisbane | Hybrid working

There are some HR contracts where you step into a perfectly polished environment, with every system, process and workflow already humming along.

This isn't one of them - and that's part of the opportunity.

We're partnering with a national transport and tourism organisation looking for an experienced HR Administrator or Coordinator to join its People & Culture team for an initial six week contract, with a strong possibility of extending to approximately three months – ASAP start.

Supporting a geographically dispersed, 24/7 operational workforce, this is a genuinely hands-on role within a People & Culture function currently going through a period of change and improvement.

Some processes remain manual, there are plenty of spreadsheets, and there is real work underway to strengthen the HR foundations of the business.

You'll come in to take ownership of much of the day-to-day HR administration, freeing up the HR lead to focus on the broader work ahead.

What you'll be doing
Your days will be varied, but will include:

  • Preparing employment contracts and managing onboarding and offboarding administration
  • Responding to employee enquiries and coordinating queries through to the appropriate team
  • Supporting recruitment activity, including interview coordination, participating in interviews and reference checking
  • Maintaining employee records, documentation and HR administration
  • Coordinating straightforward performance and employee relations processes, including documentation and meeting support
  • Supporting managers with the administrative components of people matters
  • Working across existing HR systems alongside some manual processes
  • Identifying opportunities to simplify, improve or automate HR processes where practical
  • Potentially supporting policy, procedure and learning initiatives depending on your experience and interests

Who we're looking for
You don't need to arrive knowing every answer, but you do need to be someone who can work things out.

You'll probably have previous experience as an HR Administrator, HR Coordinator or developing HR Advisor and be comfortable working independently once you've been given some direction.

You'll be organised, practical and happy to take ownership rather than waiting to be told what to do next.

Just as importantly, you'll need to be comfortable working in an environment where HR systems and processes are still evolving. If you need sophisticated technology and perfectly automated workflows to do your best work, this probably isn't the contract for you.

You'll suit the team particularly well if you're:

  • Confident, capable and able to use your initiative
  • Highly organised and comfortable managing competing priorities
  • Happy working across both HR administration and broader people activities
  • Comfortable asking questions when you need to, then getting on with the job
  • Approachable, down to earth and able to have a bit of fun along the way
  • Interested in improving processes rather than simply working around them
  • Comfortable supporting a geographically dispersed and operational workforce
  • Are available for immediate start

Experience supporting recruitment or straightforward employee relations matters would be valuable, but neither needs to be your specialty.

Why consider it?
For someone who enjoys getting into the detail, making things easier and being genuinely useful to a busy HR leader, there's an opportunity to make an impact very quickly.

You'll also have:

  • Initial six week contract with likely extension to approximately three months
  • Hybrid working – three days in the office and two from home
  • Tuesday and Wednesday as team office days, with flexibility around your third day
  • Corporate office hours with flexible start and finish times
  • East Pinkenba location with onsite parking
  • A relaxed, approachable and down to earth team environment
  • Exposure across recruitment, employee relations, HR operations and process improvement

The role is Brisbane based and we're looking for someone who can start quickly.

If you're an experienced HR Administrator or Coordinator who likes rolling up your sleeves, bringing some order to the moving parts and helping a team get things done, I'd love to hear from you.

job.title: HR Business Partner - Love Hands-On, People-Focused HR?
job.description:
Human Resources Business Partner

Cannon Hill | $110,000 – $120,000 + Super | Full-time Onsite

Do you love HR that's genuinely about people?


For some HR professionals, the most rewarding part of the job is being there when a leader needs advice. Helping an employee work through an issue. Getting out from behind the desk, understanding what's happening in the operation and finding a practical way forward.

If that's the kind of HR you enjoy, this opportunity could be a great fit.

We are partnering with a large, established Australian beef processing and manufacturing business employing more than 1,100 people at its Brisbane operation.

It's a busy, hands-on, multicultural and highly operational workplace – and we're looking for an experienced HR professional who genuinely enjoys supporting the people who make a business work.

About the role
Reporting to the People & Culture Manager, you'll provide hands-on HR support to leaders and employees across a large operational workforce.

This isn't a role where HR sits separately from the business. You'll be visible, accessible and actively building relationships across the operation.

Your day could include:

  • Supporting leaders with employee relations, conduct and performance matters
  • Managing grievances, investigations and workplace issues
  • Coaching managers through difficult conversations and people decisions
  • Supporting attendance and absenteeism matters
  • Interpreting policies, Awards, industrial instruments and employment legislation
  • Preparing employment documentation and maintaining accurate HR records
  • Supporting onboarding, employee changes and exits
  • Working with Payroll, Safety, Return to Work and operational teams
  • Helping leaders become more confident managing their own people
  • Contributing to improved HR processes, systems and ways of working

Most importantly, you'll provide a responsive and practical HR service to the business and its people.

Who will thrive here?
We're looking for someone who genuinely likes operational HR.

Someone approachable enough that employees feel comfortable talking to them, but confident enough to have difficult conversations and provide clear advice when needed.

You'll ideally bring:

  • A minimum of five years' generalist HR experience, ideally as an HR Advisor, Senior HR Advisor or HR Business Partner
  • A qualification in Human Resources, Business or a related discipline
  • Strong employee relations and performance management experience
  • Working knowledge of Australian employment legislation, Awards and the Fair Work Act
  • Confidence coaching and supporting frontline leaders
  • Strong relationship-building and communication skills
  • A practical, service-oriented approach to HR
  • Resilience and the ability to remain calm in a busy operational environment
  • A willingness to roll up your sleeves and help where needed

Experience within food or meat manufacturing, FMCG, logistics, transport, warehousing, construction or another blue-collar operational environment would be highly regarded.

You must also hold unrestricted Australian working rights.

The working environment
We want to be transparent about this because finding the right environment matters just as much as finding the right role.

This is a beef processing and manufacturing operation. It's a large industrial site and HR works closely with the employees and leaders who keep that operation running.

You'll be joining an incredibly diverse workforce representing more than 70 nationalities, with many long-serving employees and a strong sense of pride in the work they do.

This is also a full-time onsite role. Being present and accessible to employees is an important part of the job, although reasonable flexibility is available when life requires it.

The hours
The HR team provides coverage across the operation through two shifts, which rotate monthly:

  • Morning shift: currently 6:00am – 2:00pm
  • Afternoon shift: 12:00pm – 8:00pm

There is an intention for the morning shift to move to a later start in the future; however, candidates should apply on the basis that the current 6:00am start remains in place.

What's on offer?

  • $110,000 – $120,000 + superannuation
  • Free onsite parking
  • Employee discounts on premium beef products
  • Exposure to a large and diverse operational workforce
  • An opportunity to broaden your ER and operational HR capability
  • A supportive People & Culture team
  • The opportunity to contribute to improving HR processes and ways of working
  • A stable Australian business operating within an essential industry

The successful candidate will also be required to complete a pre-employment medical and Q Fever screening/vaccination as part of the employment process.

Interested?
If you're a practical HR professional who gets genuine satisfaction from supporting people, building relationships and providing a great HR service to an operational business, we'd love to hear from you.

To apply
Please apply with current resume in Microsoft Word format only (.doc or .docx) through the application portal. If you would like to have a confidential discussion, please contact Taylah Gurney at taylah.gurney@davidsonwp.com. Want to know more about Davidson? Visit us at www.davidsonwp.com

job.title: Partner - Executive Search
job.description:
You’ve built your reputation. What do you want to build next?

You know executive search. You’ve built trusted relationships, developed a strong network and earned credibility with senior leaders.

Now you may be looking for more autonomy, more opportunity to shape your market and a platform that backs you to keep building.

As a Partner | Executive Search with Davidson Executive & Talent, you’ll lead senior appointments, grow trusted client relationships and help shape our executive search capability nationally.

About Davidson

For 35 years, Davidson has helped organisations make better decisions about their people, capability and future direction.

Today, we bring together expertise across strategy, people and technology.

Within Davidson Executive & Talent, we partner with organisations to secure and support specialist talent, from early career professionals through to executive and board leaders.

The opportunity

This is a senior role with genuine autonomy.

You’ll work directly with chief executive officers, boards and executive leaders on appointments where experience and judgement matter. You’ll own your client relationships; lead retained search assignments and build a portfolio around your strengths and network.

You’ll also influence how our executive search capability grows, while drawing on the relationships and expertise across Davidson.

You’ll:

  • Lead C-suite, board and senior executive search assignments.
  • Build and grow a sustainable portfolio of retained search clients.
  • Advise senior leaders on roles, markets and leadership requirements.
  • Develop search strategies and lead assignments from briefing through to appointment.
  • Bring market insight, sound judgement and structured assessment to every search.
  • Build relationships that lead to repeat work and long-term partnerships.
  • Share relationships, opportunities and expertise across Davidson.

What you’ll bring

You’re an established executive search or senior recruitment professional who knows how to build a market, not just deliver an assignment.

You’ll bring:

  • Strong executive search or senior recruitment experience.
  • Credibility with chief executive officers, boards and senior leaders.
  • A track record of winning work and developing lasting client relationships.
  • An established professional network.
  • Commercial acumen and confidence developing new opportunities.
  • Strong assessment, stakeholder management and advisory skills.
  • Sound judgement, integrity and a genuine commitment to candidate care.

Most importantly, you know that great executive search is built on trust, good judgement and relationships that last.

Why Davidson?

You’ve already proven you can build a successful career. We’ll give you the room to keep building it.

You’ll have autonomy to shape your market, direct access to senior leaders and opportunities to collaborate across our whole team Davidson Executive & Talent, Davidson Strategy & Performance and Davidson Technology Consulting.

You’ll also have genuine flexibility, development opportunities and recognition for individual and team contributions.

And we make time to enjoy the wins, with high achievers’ lunches, monthly celebration hours, values awards, steak and chips nights, and an annual sales incentive trip for top performers.

Ready for what’s next?

If you want the freedom to build trusted client relationships, lead important appointments and have a voice in the future of Davidson Executive & Talent, we’d like to meet you.

Apply now to start the conversation.

job.title: Rostering Coordinator
job.description:
About the Company

Davidson is partnering with a well-established not-for-profit organisation delivering essential aged care services across the community.

With a strong focus on helping people remain independent and supported in their own homes, this is an organisation where the work happening behind the scenes directly impacts the quality of care clients receive every day.

You'll be joining a supportive and collaborative team that genuinely cares about delivering a great service to both their clients and the care staff working throughout the community.

About the Role

If you're someone who enjoys a busy environment, loves solving problems and gets satisfaction from making all the moving pieces fit together, this could be a great next step.

We're looking for an experienced Rostering Coordinator to join the team on a permanent, full-time basis in Indooroopilly.

Sitting at the heart of day-to-day operations, you'll coordinate care staff and client schedules to ensure the right people are in the right place at the right time. Plans will change, people will call in sick, shifts will need to be filled and priorities will move throughout the day. You'll be the person finding solutions and keeping everything on track.

Your day will include:

  • Building and maintaining care staff rosters and client schedules
  • Managing sick calls, leave, cancellations and last-minute roster changes
  • Filling vacant shifts and finding solutions to gaps in coverage
  • Communicating regularly with care staff, clients and internal teams
  • Balancing client requirements with staff availability and operational needs
  • Maintaining accurate roster and workforce information across internal systems
  • Working closely with the wider team to ensure clients receive consistent and reliable care

This isn't a role where you'll spend your day quietly working through an inbox. It's hands-on, people-focused and constantly moving. You'll be communicating throughout the day, making decisions and managing multiple priorities at once.

For someone who genuinely enjoys rostering and the challenge of pulling everything together, there is plenty here to keep you engaged.

About You

We're looking for someone who understands the moving parts involved in rostering, scheduling or workforce coordination and can confidently step into a busy environment.

You'll ideally bring:

  • Previous experience in rostering, scheduling, allocations or workforce coordination
  • Experience managing high-volume rosters with frequent changes
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to think on your feet
  • Confidence managing competing priorities without losing attention to detail
  • Excellent communication skills and a professional, personable approach
  • Confidence communicating with employees, clients and internal stakeholders via phone and email
  • Strong systems capability, with experience using Sandwai highly regarded
  • Previous experience within aged care, home care, disability, healthcare or community services highly regarded

Most importantly, you're someone who takes ownership. When the roster changes unexpectedly, you don't just identify the problem. You start working on the solution.

The Benefits

  • Permanent, full-time opportunity offering long-term stability
  • Access to not-for-profit salary packaging, helping you maximise your take-home pay
  • Convenient Indooroopilly location
  • Join an established and respected organisation within the aged care sector
  • Supportive and collaborative team environment
  • Play an important role in supporting the delivery of care within the community
  • Varied position with plenty of opportunity to problem-solve and take ownership
  • Build on your experience within the growing aged care and community services sector
  • Street parking available with limited onsite parking

If you're an experienced Scheduler looking for a role where you'll be trusted to take ownership, solve problems and genuinely contribute to the delivery of quality care, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: Senior Advisor (Capability) A06
job.description:
About the Company

RoadTek operates within the Queensland Department of Transport and Main Roads, supporting the delivery of transport infrastructure across Queensland.

This opportunity sits within RoadTek’s capability function and will contribute to the development and improvement of learning materials designed to support its workforce.

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced AO5 Senior Capability Advisor to develop and enhance face-to-face, blended and online learning solutions for RoadTek’s workforce.

This is a hands-on design and development role where you will uplift existing eLearning courses and create new learning materials. Your work will include eLearning content, presentation slides, facilitator resources, learner materials, activities, assessments and visual learning assets.

Working under the direction of the Senior Advisor, Capability, you will manage allocated tasks autonomously while collaborating closely with the instructional design team, subject matter experts and business stakeholders.

You will use your instructional design expertise and creativity to translate workplace learning requirements into clear, practical and engaging learning experiences.

About You

To be successful in this role, you will bring two to five years of professional instructional design experience, together with demonstrated experience developing adult workplace learning.

You will also bring:

  • Strong written communication and visual design capability
  • Practical experience with eLearning authoring tools such as Articulate Rise and Storyline
  • Strong stakeholder collaboration and negotiation skills
  • The ability to work autonomously while contributing effectively within a collaborative team
  • The ability to develop engaging learning resources across digital, blended and face-to-face formats

Experience using Canva will be desirable, while candidates with strong visual design skills and the demonstrated ability to quickly learn new design skills will be highly regarded.

A qualification in Training Design and Development or an equivalent discipline is highly desirable. Experience developing learning for blue-collar, operational, construction, infrastructure, transport, trade or safety-focused workforces will also be highly regarded.

Please note: Applicants must submit a portfolio containing images or screenshots of their work and clearly explain their personal level of involvement in each example.

The Benefits

This opportunity offers the chance to apply your instructional design expertise in a practical workforce environment while contributing to learning solutions across multiple delivery formats.

You will benefit from:

  • Flexible work location within Queensland
  • A varied, hands-on instructional design role
  • The opportunity to work across eLearning, blended and face-to-face learning
  • Collaboration with instructional designers, subject matter experts and key business stakeholders
  • The opportunity to create learning solutions for an operational workforce

job.title: AO5 Procurement and Contracts Officer
job.description:
About the Company

The Office of Industrial Relations (OIR) leads, promotes and enables improvements in work health and safety across Queensland, while supporting effective workers’ compensation regulatory services and a fair industrial relations framework.

The Finance, Facilities & Procurement unit sits within OIR’s Corporate Directorate and delivers a range of corporate services, including financial management, procurement and contracts, and facilities management.



About the Role

OIR is seeking an experienced Procurement & Contracts Officer for an initial six-month engagement based at 1 William Street, Brisbane.

Working within the Finance, Facilities & Procurement unit, you will primarily support Learning & Development procurement activities, while also assisting with broader procurement requirements and associated administration across OIR.

  • Providing procurement advice and support across planning, sourcing, evaluation, contract negotiation, formation, management and administration.
  • Advising stakeholders on Queensland Government and agency procurement policies, practices, processes and templates.
  • Preparing procurement and evaluation plans, sourcing documentation and briefing notes for senior and executive management.
  • Supporting stakeholders to develop specifications and appropriate procurement strategies that deliver value for money.
  • Assisting with requests for quotes, tenders, contracts and associated procurement documentation.
  • Preparing purchase requisitions and coordinating vendor creations and extensions through SAP.
  • Liaising with Queensland Shared Services, Finance and Budgeting teams to resolve procurement, purchase order and vendor matters.
  • Supporting the central OIR Procurement inbox and associated records management using SharePoint Online and shared drives.

cohealth is a not-for-profit community health organisation delivering health and support services across Melbourne’s CBD, northern and western suburbs, and the East Coast of Tasmania. You will shape financial strategy, oversee organisation-wide budgeting, forecasting and reporting, and provide the analysis and advice that supports sound strategic and investment decisions. Beyond traditional finance leadership, you will strengthen enterprise risk and assurance, drive effective stewardship of assets and resources, and build a contemporary business partnering approach that strengthens financial accountability and capability across cohealth.

You will be an accomplished senior finance executive with experience leading within a complex, multi-program and multi-site environment and the credibility to influence CEOs, Boards and senior leaders. A tertiary qualification in Finance, Accounting, Commerce or a related discipline and CA or CPA qualification are essential, supported by substantial capability across financial strategy, governance, reporting, internal controls, enterprise risk, internal audit and organisational assurance. Experience within government-funded, health, community, not-for-profit or service delivery environments will be highly regarded, alongside exposure to property, assets or procurement portfolios. You will bring strong commercial judgement and the ability to translate complex financial information into clear choices and action. Equally important will be your collaborative leadership style, ability to build financial confidence among non-finance leaders, and genuine alignment with cohealth’s values, mission and commitment to stewarding resources for the benefit of communities experiencing inequality.

job.title: Program Manager - Centre For Eye Research
job.description:
• Play a pivotal role in advancing world-leading eye research through strategic operational leadership
  • Partner with leading researchers and clinicians to translate scientific ambition into real-world impact
  • Shape a high-performing research environment through stronger systems, collaboration and continuous improvement

The Centre for Eye Research Australia (CERA) is an internationally recognised medical research institute dedicated to preventing vision loss through discovery science, clinical research, public health and translation. Working in close partnership with the University of Melbourne, hospitals and industry, CERA brings together world class researchers and clinicians to improve eye health outcomes and deliver real world impact. With multidisciplinary programs spanning basic science through to clinical research, CERA continues to operate at the forefront of innovation, improving diagnosis, prevention and treatment of eye disease.




The Program Manager role has been created to drive major collaborative research initiatives that bring together leading clinicians, scientists and partners to tackle the biggest challenges in eye health. This role will help shape CERA’s future research portfolio by enabling larger, more connected and more ambitious funding opportunities.




Reporting to the Co-Chief Operating Officer and working in close partnership with and under the guidance of the Managing Director, the Program Manager provides operational leadership across designated research programs. The role works in close alignment with the Deputy Director and Clinical Research Leads. Acting as a critical connector between Clinical Research Leads and research support services teams, you will help build a more integrated and collaborative research environment. You will identify opportunities to align expertise across research programs, co-ordinate across functions (including finance, HR, research governance), support compliance and risk management as well as foster strategic partnerships, coordinate major research initiatives and position CERA to compete successfully for larger multi-disciplinary grants and funding opportunities. You will also facilitate translating research strategies into operational plans, oversee program delivery, manage budgets and grant expenditure, and strengthen workforce capability. This role is designed to allow Clinical Research Leads to focus on scientific leadership, while ensuring programs are well managed, sustainable and positioned for success.




To be successful in this role you will bring a postgraduate qualification within science, health, biomedical science or a related discipline, combined with demonstrated experience leading complex, multidisciplinary programs. You will have strong project management and organisational capability, with proven operational management experience within research, healthcare, higher education or similarly complex environments. You thrive on improving systems and processes to lift organisational effectiveness, bringing a strong financial and delivery mindset. A credible and emotionally intelligent leader, you are comfortable influencing without authority, building trust with clinicians and researchers, and driving outcomes through collaboration. You combine sound judgement and resilience with a hands-on approach, moving seamlessly between strategic planning and operational delivery to enable research excellence.

job.title: AO4 Land Research Officer
job.description:
About the Company

Davidson is partnering with the Department of Natural Resources and Mines, Manufacturing and Regional and Rural Development, a Queensland Government department focused on strengthening regions, economies and partnerships across the state.

The department works collaboratively with communities, industry and government stakeholders to support Queensland’s land, resources, manufacturing and regional sectors. It is committed to a safe, inclusive and respectful workplace, underpinned by a people-first, collaborative and innovative culture.


About the Role

We are seeking an AO4 Land Research Officer to join the State Interests team in Brisbane. This role supports work that enables connection to country and access to land for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, including matters relating to native title, land transfers and Indigenous Land Use Agreements.

You will undertake detailed land tenure research and analysis, working with spatial information specialists and other stakeholders to provide accurate information supporting native title claims, compensation claims and associated negotiations.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Undertaking land tenure research, analysis and interpretation.
  • Collating tenure, mapping and other information relevant to native title and compensation matters and Indigenous Land Use Agreements.
  • Providing accurate research to support the determination of land tenure matters and escalating complex or sensitive issues where required.
  • Preparing and contributing to briefs, reports and court documents.
  • Researching, interpreting and applying relevant legislation, policies and procedures.
  • Supporting engagement with government agencies, the National Native Title Tribunal, Indigenous groups, industry bodies and members of the public.
  • Maintaining accurate records and producing reports and statistical information using departmental databases and information systems.
  • Working collaboratively across the team, including undertaking peer review and supporting colleagues with relevant systems and processes.


About You

You will bring strong research, analytical and problem-solving skills, together with the ability to interpret detailed information and communicate effectively with a diverse range of stakeholders.

To succeed in this role, you will demonstrate:

  • Strong research, analytical and problem-solving capability.
  • Well-developed written and verbal communication skills.
  • The ability to interpret and implement legislation, policy and procedures.
  • Confidence using, or the ability to quickly learn, information and database systems.
  • A collaborative approach and commitment to equity, diversity, respect and inclusion.
  • Willingness and ability to travel, including to rural and remote locations where required.

Experience or an interest in planning, environmental science or management, spatial science, business, law or project management will be well regarded.

Experience engaging with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, along with experience using Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and other digital applications, is highly desirable.

You must hold a current driver’s licence or be able to obtain one within six months of commencement and be eligible to work in Australia.


The Benefits

This is an opportunity to apply your research and analytical skills to meaningful work with a Queensland Government department while contributing to important land tenure and native title outcomes.

The assignment offers:

  • Contract: 31 August 2026 to 31 August 2027.
  • Extension: Option for a further 12 months.
  • Location: 1 William Street, Brisbane.
  • Hours: 40 hours per week, with standard business hours between 8:00am and 5:00pm Monday to Friday.
  • Exposure to complex land tenure, native title and Indigenous land matters.
  • The opportunity to work with a diverse range of government, industry and community stakeholders.
  • A collaborative, inclusive and respectful working environment.

If you are an analytical and detail-focused professional with an interest in land tenure, legislation and research, we encourage you to apply.


How to Apply

job.title: Policy & Advocacy Manager - Australian Energy Council
job.description:
• Shape national retail energy policy and strengthen AEC’s voice with government, regulators and industry
  • Turn complex regulatory issues into clear, compelling positions that influence energy reform
  • Build member consensus and help AEC move from reactive submissions to proactive advocacy

The Australian Energy Council (AEC) is the peak body representing leading energy retailers and generators operating across Australia. Its members supply energy to more than 10 million homes and businesses and play a critical role in delivering a reliable, affordable and increasingly decarbonised energy system.

Through policy advocacy, industry engagement and thought leadership, AEC works with governments, regulators, market bodies and consumer representatives to shape the future of Australia’s energy market. As the sector undergoes significant change, AEC is strengthening its ability to engage earlier, build consensus and contribute proactively to national energy reform.

About the Role:

Reporting to the General Manager Retail Policy, the Policy & Advocacy Manager will connect policy development, member engagement and external advocacy across AEC’s retail agenda. Working closely with other senior members of the AEC team, you will turn complex regulatory and market issues into clear, evidence-based positions that influence decision-makers.

Key priorities will include:

  • Leading engagement with AEC’s Retail Working Group, synthesising specialist member input and building alignment around shared priorities.
  • Building trusted relationships with members, policymakers, regulators, market bodies and consumer representatives.
  • Identifying emerging retail policy issues and progressing proactive reform across areas such as consumer pricing, consumer protections and consumer energy resources.
  • Developing advocacy strategies and working with policy and communications colleagues to produce submissions, briefings and compelling external narratives.

About You

You will be a relationship-led energy professional who can engage credibly with experienced policy and regulatory stakeholders while remaining comfortable with complexity and detail. You may not be a career policy specialist, but you will be able to quickly understand technical concepts, identify what matters and communicate a clear and persuasive position.

You will bring:

  • Experience within the energy sector, ideally gained in a retailer, market body, regulator, government agency, peak body or consumer organisation.
  • A sound understanding of policy or regulatory processes and the ability to analyse complex technical, legal or commercial information.
  • Demonstrated stakeholder engagement and influencing capability, including experience building consensus across differing perspectives.
  • Strong written and verbal communication, sound judgement and the ability to prioritise and manage competing outcomes across diverse stakeholder groups.

This is an opportunity to join a small, highly influential organisation and help shape policy outcomes affecting Australia’s energy retailers, consumers and broader energy transition.
