job.title: Testing & Commissioning Manager
job.description:
About the Company

Iberdrola Australia is delivering major energy infrastructure that will support the continued development and resilience of Australia’s electricity network.

This position will contribute to the Victoria to New South Wales Interconnector West project, working across a complex program of transmission line and terminal station works. The project involves multiple contractors, network operators, equipment manufacturers and regulatory stakeholders.

About the Role

The Testing & Commissioning Manager will lead the development of the project’s overarching testing and commissioning strategy.

Joining during the development phase, you will influence how assets are designed, procured, factory tested, installed, commissioned and ultimately energised. You will establish the commissioning philosophy, sequencing, packaging approach, outage strategy and system integration requirements across the project lifecycle.

You will provide owner-side oversight and technical assurance across:

  • 500 kV overhead transmission lines and terminal stations
  • Primary plant, STATCOMs, shunt reactors and capacitor banks
  • Protection, control, SCADA, communications and metering systems
  • Factory acceptance testing, site acceptance testing and pre-commissioning
  • Outage planning, switching, energisation and operational handover
  • Integrated and inter-regional system testing

Working closely with Design & Construction contractors, OEMs, AEMO, TNSPs, VicGrid and operational teams, you will review and challenge commissioning plans, coordinate network interfaces and ensure activities meet technical, contractual, safety and program requirements.

This is a senior leadership opportunity for an engineer who can set the standard, develop effective contractor relationships and confidently challenge technical approaches where required.

About You

You are an experienced Testing & Commissioning professional with a strong background in high-voltage transmission infrastructure and a detailed understanding of the complete asset lifecycle - from design and procurement through construction, testing, energisation and handover.

You will bring

  • A Bachelor of Engineering in Electrical Engineering, Power Systems or an equivalent discipline
  • At least eight years’ experience in high-voltage transmission testing and commissioning
  • Experience with systems operating above 275 kV, ideally at 400 kV or 500 kV
  • Demonstrated experience across substations, transmission lines and integrated systems
  • Knowledge of FAT, SAT, inspection and test plans, pre-energisation and completion processes
  • Experience coordinating outages and energisation within operational networks
  • Working knowledge of AEMO processes, grid compliance frameworks and Australian Standards
  • Experience with IEC 61850 and process bus implementation
  • The ability to manage contractors, review programs and challenge technical submissions
  • Strong stakeholder engagement, communication, safety and risk-management capability

Australian network experience and familiarity with AEMO requirements will be highly regarded. Candidates with relevant network authorisations, HV switching or access permits, construction industry tickets or high-risk safety training will also be viewed favourably.

The Benefits

  • Senior strategic role on a significant Australian transmission project
  • Opportunity to shape testing and commissioning from development through energisation
  • Broad technical exposure across transmission lines, terminal stations and integrated systems
  • Melbourne-based position with travel to regional Victorian sites
  • Potential overseas travel to support factory acceptance testing
  • High level of influence across contractors, suppliers, network operators and project leadership

This role will suit a technically credible and commercially aware leader who is motivated by complex infrastructure, system-wide testing and the safe transition of major electrical assets into operation.

job.title: HR Project Specialist – Integration
job.description:
2–3 Month Contract | $94.88 per hour + super | Brisbane or Gympie

An opportunity has become available for an experienced HR professional to join a well-established Australian organisation for a short-term integration project following a business acquisition.

Working closely with the People & Culture team, you will play a hands-on role in understanding and documenting the acquired business's current people processes, identifying differences and opportunities, and developing practical recommendations to support integration into the broader organisation.

This is a great contract for an experienced HR practitioner who enjoys project work, can quickly make sense of an existing HR environment and is comfortable moving between analysis, recommendations and hands-on implementation.

The role

A key focus will be reviewing and mapping current Hire-to-Retire processes and policies across the acquired business and comparing these against the broader organisation's existing P&C framework.

You will help determine what needs to change, where priorities sit and the most practical sequence and approach for integration.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Mapping current-state HR processes and policies across the employee lifecycle
  • Reviewing and comparing existing processes against the broader P&C framework
  • Identifying gaps, inconsistencies and opportunities for alignment
  • Developing practical recommendations around integration priorities, sequencing and approach
  • Supporting the completion of outstanding people-related due diligence activities
  • Assisting with the rollout of updated policies, processes and training materials
  • Working collaboratively with P&C and operational stakeholders to support a practical and considered transition

About you

We are looking for an experienced HR professional who can quickly get across a business, ask the right questions and turn information into clear, practical recommendations.

You may come from an HR Business Partner, Senior HR Advisor, HR Project or P&C Project background and will ideally bring:

  • Strong generalist HR knowledge across the employee lifecycle
  • Experience with HR projects, process improvement, integration or transformation
  • Strong process mapping, documentation and analytical capability
  • The ability to identify gaps and translate findings into practical recommendations
  • Confidence working autonomously and managing competing priorities
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills
  • A pragmatic, hands-on approach and willingness to support implementation as required

Previous experience supporting an acquisition or business integration would be highly regarded but is not essential.

The opportunity
This is an immediate 2–3 month contract, paying $94.88 per hour + super.

The role can be based from Brisbane or Gympie, however regular travel to the Gympie site will be required for Brisbane-based candidates.

If you're an experienced HR professional available for your next contract and enjoy getting into the detail, improving how things work and helping businesses navigate change, we'd love to hear from you.

job.description:
• ​​Shape development outcomes in one of Queensland's fastest-growing cities​
  • ​​Lead complex negotiations, quality uplift and business improvement​
  • ​​9-day fortnight, flexible work and genuine pathway to leadership​

The City of Logan is one of Australia’s fastest-growing communities, driven by major infrastructure investment, rapid population growth, and its exciting role as a co-host city for the 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games. The City of Logan is entering an exciting new phase with big picture thinkers helping shape the future. There’s purpose in our step and fresh energy in the air, with a focus on delivering exceptional service and value for money – with heart.




As part of this exciting growth, Logan Water plays a vital role in shaping the city’s future. Established as a Directorate of Logan City Council, Logan Water delivers essential water and wastewater services that enable the city to thrive while safeguarding the sustainability of our natural resources. Responsible for $4 billion in assets, generating $270 million in annual revenue, and managing around $350 million in capital and operational expenditure each year, Logan Water is a cornerstone of the city’s success. With a vision to be reliable, sustainable, and committed, we remain focused on providing safe, dependable, and environmentally responsible water and sewerage services for the benefit of the entire Logan community.




Reporting to the Water Development Services Assessment Team Leader, the Principal Development Assessment Engineer is a pivotal technical role within Logan Water's Development Services Program. At a time of significant growth and transformation, this position will play a key role in shaping how Logan Water assesses, supports and enables development across one of Queensland's fastest-growing communities.




As the senior technical specialist, you will provide expert guidance on complex water and wastewater development assessment matters, while driving quality assurance, capability uplift and continuous improvement across the function. A key focus of the role will be leading the assessment of complex development applications, negotiating infrastructure and tankering agreements, and resolving challenging technical and commercial issues with developers, consultants, government agencies and industry stakeholders. You will bring a balanced and pragmatic approach to development outcomes, combining strong engineering judgement with exceptional stakeholder engagement and negotiation skills to achieve outcomes that support both community expectations and sustainable growth.




This role will also play a significant part in Logan Water's business improvement journey. Working closely with leadership, you will contribute to the development of quality assurance frameworks, decision-making tools, customer-facing guidance, onboarding and competency programs, and a range of initiatives designed to enhance service delivery, consistency and operational performance. Your ability to identify opportunities, influence change and translate technical expertise into practical improvements will be critical to success.




To be considered for this opportunity, you will bring extensive experience in water and wastewater development assessment, infrastructure planning, land development or related engineering environments. You will possess strong technical knowledge of the development assessment process, water and sewer infrastructure planning principles, and the broader development industry. Equally important will be your ability to coach others, manage complex stakeholder relationships, navigate sensitive negotiations and drive continuous improvement outcomes.




This is a unique opportunity to join a growing organisation at a pivotal stage of its evolution. Offering a nine-day fortnight, flexible work arrangements, ongoing professional development and exposure to some of South-East Queensland's most significant growth and infrastructure challenges, this role provides the chance to make a lasting impact on the future of Logan Water and the communities it serves.

job.title: Director Planning, Growth & Sustainability – Cairns Council
job.description:
• Shape the future growth of one of Australia’s most iconic regions
  • Lead a diverse planning, growth and sustainability portfolio
  • Executive influence, community impact and an exceptional Cairns lifestyle

Cairns is a region of extraordinary significance and opportunity. Home to more than 170,000 people and positioned between two World Heritage areas, the Great Barrier Reef and the Wet Tropics rainforest, the region combines strong population growth, economic opportunity and an enviable lifestyle with a complex and highly valued natural environment.

Cairns Regional Council plays a central role in balancing these opportunities and responsibilities, planning for growth while protecting the qualities that make the region such a distinctive place to live, work, invest and visit.

The Planning, Growth & Sustainability Directorate is at the heart of this agenda. Spanning strategic and statutory planning, development assessment, sustainability, growth management, regulatory services and compliance, the Directorate helps shape how Cairns grows and how Council responds to the changing needs of its community.

Reporting directly to the CEO and joining a cohesive and highly engaged Executive Leadership Team, the Director Planning, Growth & Sustainability will lead a multidisciplinary Directorate of approximately 100 people. This is a broad and influential executive mandate. The Director will provide strategic leadership across the region’s planning and growth agenda while ensuring high-quality, responsive and customer-focused delivery across the Directorate’s regulatory and operational functions.

Working at the intersection of community expectations, development, environmental stewardship and government policy, you will help navigate some of the most important decisions shaping the future of Cairns.

You will provide trusted advice to the CEO, Mayor and Councillors, build productive relationships with government, industry, developers and community stakeholders, and represent Council in significant planning, development and regulatory matters.

Equally important will be your leadership of people and performance. You will continue to build capability across the Directorate, foster an engaged and accountable culture, encourage innovation and continuous improvement, and ensure strong governance, financial management, risk and safety practices.

To be successful in this role, you will bring extensive leadership and management experience within large organisations, with the judgement, credibility and resilience to operate effectively in a complex and highly visible environment. Your experience may have been developed within local or state government, a regional authority, or another complex organisation with significant planning, development, regulatory, growth or sustainability responsibilities.

You will bring strong knowledge of Queensland’s planning and regulatory environment, together with a demonstrated ability to translate strategy and policy into tangible organisational and community outcomes. Comfortable navigating competing priorities and diverse stakeholder interests, you will understand how to operate effectively within a political environment while providing considered, pragmatic and trusted advice.

A strong people leader, you will have experience leading and developing multidisciplinary professional teams and creating cultures characterised by accountability, collaboration and high performance. Your commercial, financial, governance and risk acumen will complement a contemporary and inclusive leadership style, enabling you to build credibility and trusted relationships across Council, government, industry and the community.

Above all, you will appreciate that successful growth is about more than planning frameworks and development decisions. It requires sound judgement, an ability to bring people with you, and a commitment to achieving enduring outcomes for the community.

About the Role

Your other responsibilities will include:

  • Performing system, integration, and end-to-end testing across Workday, UKG, and Dayforce.

job.description:
• Lead strategic procurement that delivers value, innovation and impact as part of the Corporate Strategy
  • Drive procurement governance, capability and organisational change
  • Enable better community outcomes through strategic procurement decisions

Moonee Valley is recognised as a great place to live, work and visit, located in Melbourne’s north west and serving more than 130,000 residents and over 10,000 local businesses. As a dynamic and diverse municipality, Council delivers a broad portfolio of services, infrastructure and strategic initiatives that support the wellbeing and prosperity of its community. Bringing together diverse professional expertise, perspectives and lived experiences, the organisation is focused on innovation, collaboration and delivering high-quality, future-focused outcomes for its community.

Reporting to the Manager Assets, EPMO & Procurement, the Head of Strategic Procurement is a key leadership role with the opportunity to shape how Moonee Valley approaches its commercial and procurement agenda. More than leading the procurement function, this role requires a broad understanding of Council’s operating environment, strategic priorities and the commercial opportunities and challenges facing the organisation. You will bring an enterprise-wide perspective to procurement, ensuring sourcing strategies, commercial decisions and supplier relationships support Council’s objectives and the delivery of MV2040 and its newly established Corporate Strategy.

Leading a specialist procurement team, you will provide strategic commercial advice across a diverse portfolio spanning infrastructure, capital works, services and corporate procurement. You will identify emerging strategic sourcing and market trends, anticipate supply and commercial risks, and translate these insights into practical strategies that improve value, resilience and organisational outcomes. With oversight of strategic sourcing, tendering, contract management, supplier engagement and procure-to-pay systems, you will continue to strengthen procurement maturity, governance and commercial capability while ensuring high standards of probity, compliance and value for money.

Central to your success will be your ability to build trusted relationships and influence across a complex stakeholder environment. Working closely with executives, senior leaders and teams across Council, you will challenge and shape thinking, navigate competing priorities and bring a strong commercial perspective to significant organisational decisions. Externally, you will develop productive relationships with suppliers, industry partners and regional government networks, identifying opportunities for collaboration, innovation and more strategic approaches to market.

The successful candidate will be an accomplished procurement and commercial leader who combines deep procurement expertise with broad organisational and commercial acumen. You will understand how procurement can enable organisational strategy rather than operate simply as a transactional or compliance function, and will bring the curiosity and judgement to understand the opportunities, constraints and changing market dynamics affecting a diverse organisation.

You will be recognised as a credible and influential advisor, capable of engaging senior stakeholders, building alignment and translating complex commercial considerations into clear recommendations and outcomes. You will bring contemporary knowledge of strategic sourcing trends, supplier markets, procurement governance and best practice, together with experience leading complex sourcing initiatives, negotiating significant contracts and strengthening procurement capability. Equally important will be your ability to lead and develop a high-performing team and create strong relationships across organisational boundaries. Experience across infrastructure, capital works and services procurement will be highly regarded, together with the judgement and stakeholder awareness required to operate effectively in a complex local government environment.

Moonee Valley City Council is proud to be an Equal Opportunity and Child Safe employer and values diversity. Applications are encouraged from people of different backgrounds, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people from culturally and linguistically diverse (CALD) backgrounds, people of any age or gender, people identifying as lesbian, gay, bisexual, trans and gender diverse, intersex and/or queer (LGBTIQA+), and people with disability. job.title: General Manager - Project Management Office
job.description:
About the Company

Our client is a large and highly regarded Australian not-for-profit organisation delivering a diverse range of essential care, community and support services.

With a long and established history, a substantial workforce and operations across multiple service areas, the organisation positively impacts tens of thousands of people each year. It is currently investing significantly in its future through a major agenda of business, operational and technology transformation.

This creates an exciting opportunity for an experienced transformation executive to join at a pivotal time and influence how strategic investment, enterprise change and innovation are delivered across the organisation.

About the Role

We are seeking an accomplished General Manager – PMO to lead the organisation's enterprise transformation portfolio, project delivery capability, innovation agenda and investment governance processes.

Reporting to a C-suite executive, this highly influential role sits at the centre of strategic decision-making and will partner closely with the Executive Leadership Team, senior leaders and key governance forums to ensure organisational investments are effectively prioritised and deliver measurable outcomes.

The mandate is to evolve the PMO into a trusted enterprise function that enables better investment decisions, strengthens portfolio performance and ensures sustainable benefits are realised from significant transformation initiatives.

Key priorities include:

  • Leading the enterprise project and transformation portfolio, improving visibility, prioritisation, and accountability.
  • Maturing portfolio management, project governance and delivery capability.
  • Providing strategic advice to executives on investment priorities, portfolio performance, organisational risk and innovation opportunities.
  • Strengthening business case evaluation, investment prioritisation, and benefits realisation.
  • Establishing pragmatic frameworks, methodologies and tools that enable effective project delivery.
  • Driving cross-functional collaboration and strengthening organisational change capability.
  • Leading and developing a capable, engaged, and respected Project Management Office team.
  • Fostering a culture of innovation, optimisation, and continuous improvement.

Success will be demonstrated through stronger alignment between strategy, investment and delivery, improved portfolio visibility and benefits realisation, and greater executive confidence in transformation outcomes.

About You

You are an experienced enterprise transformation and portfolio leader who combines strategic thinking, commercial acumen and strong delivery capability. You are comfortable operating at executive level while remaining pragmatic and close enough to delivery to understand what is really happening across a complex portfolio.

You will bring demonstrated capability across the five priority areas of enterprise transformation, portfolio leadership, PMO maturity, benefits realisation, and project delivery.

Your background will ideally include:

  • 10+ years' experience across business transformation, change management and process improvement.
  • Significant leadership and project/program management experience.
  • Direct experience leading, transforming or maturing an enterprise PMO or portfolio function.
  • Previous experience delivering large and complex transformation programs.
  • Strong portfolio and investment governance capability.
  • Executive-level stakeholder management and experience presenting to Executive Leadership Teams and Boards.
  • Strong commercial acumen with the ability to link investment decisions to measurable operational, financial and strategic outcomes.
  • The ability to influence without relying on authority and build trust across complex stakeholder groups.
  • Relevant tertiary, project management and change management qualifications.

Experience within aged care or the not-for-profit sector would be advantageous; however, proven capability in enterprise transformation, portfolio leadership and investment governance is considered more important than industry background.

The Benefits

This is a rare opportunity to take on a genuine enterprise-wide transformation mandate and shape how a large, purpose-led organisation prioritises investment and delivers significant organisational change.

The offering includes:

  • Permanent executive leadership opportunity
  • Competitive base salary plus superannuation
  • Five weeks' annual leave
  • Hybrid and flexible working arrangements
  • Attractive not-for-profit salary packaging benefits
  • Free on-site parking
  • On-site café with staff discount.

job.title: APS6 Program Officer - Sustainable Agriculture
job.description:
About the Company

Davidson is partnering with a Federal Government department to recruit an experienced APS6 Program Officer for a 12-month contract based in Brisbane CBD.

This opportunity sits within a branch responsible for delivering significant Australian Government investment in sustainable agriculture and natural resource management. The broader program supports projects designed to improve agricultural productivity, build resilience and increase natural capital across Australia.


About the Role

Working with limited guidance, you will support the effective delivery and administration of nationally significant programs and projects. The position combines program and agreement management, stakeholder engagement, governance, reporting and executive-level advice.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Assessing milestone reports, variation requests and final reports, and providing recommendations to decision-makers in accordance with relevant policies.
  • Managing agreements, including the assessment of project outputs, outcomes, annual reports and invoices.
  • Managing payments and agreement variations through departmental financial systems.
  • Engaging regularly with grantees, project partners, internal stakeholders and other government agencies.
  • Maintaining program documentation, project trackers, operating procedures and records.
  • Supporting governance, assurance, risk management and financial activities across the program.
  • Preparing high-quality advice and correspondence for executive-level stakeholders and the Minister's Office, including submissions, briefings and Senate Estimates material.
  • Reviewing program reporting data within monitoring and evaluation systems.
  • Developing and reviewing communications materials, including presentations, talking points, website content, social media material and event collateral.
  • Leading, managing and mentoring junior staff to support successful program outcomes.
  • Undertaking occasional field work in remote and regional locations.

About You

You will be an experienced program professional who can confidently manage moderately complex work, exercise sound judgement and deliver high-quality outcomes with limited guidance.

To succeed in this role, you will demonstrate:

  • Strong program, project or agreement management capability.
  • Experience assessing reports, deliverables, variations and financial information against established policies and requirements.
  • Excellent written communication skills, with the ability to prepare concise executive and ministerial-level advice.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills and confidence working across internal and external stakeholder groups.
  • Sound judgement, attention to detail and the ability to manage competing priorities.
  • Experience supporting governance, assurance, risk and financial management activities.
  • Leadership capability, including experience supporting or mentoring junior team members.
  • An ability to engage confidently with subject matter relating to agriculture, science, engineering, geography, media and communications, or similar disciplines.
  • The ability to obtain and maintain a Baseline security clearance.


The Benefits

  • Competitive rate of $65 - $70 per hour + super.
  • 12-month Federal Government contract.
  • Convenient Brisbane CBD location.
  • Flexible working arrangements.
  • Opportunity to contribute to nationally significant programs supporting sustainable agriculture, resilience and Australia's natural capital.
  • Varied role spanning program delivery, stakeholder engagement, executive advice and communications.

job.title: Principal Investigator – Workplace Conduct
job.description:
About the Company
Davidson is partnering with a Queensland Government organisation to recruit an experienced Principal Investigator – Conduct Investigations for an initial 6-month contract.

This is an opportunity to join an established conduct investigations function and manage sensitive and potentially complex workplace conduct matters within a large government environment.

About the Role
As Principal Investigator, you will independently manage a caseload of workplace conduct investigations from commencement through to findings and reporting.

Working within relevant legislative, policy and governance frameworks, you will assess allegations and evidence, conduct interviews, analyse information and prepare clear, defensible investigation reports and recommendations.

Key responsibilities will include:

  • Independently managing sensitive and complex workplace conduct investigations
  • Managing multiple active investigation matters and associated casework
  • Gathering, assessing and analysing evidence and relevant information
  • Conducting interviews with relevant parties and witnesses
  • Applying procedural fairness throughout the investigation process
  • Preparing high-quality investigation reports, findings, briefs and recommendations
  • Providing advice on conduct, complaints and investigation matters
  • Identifying emerging or systemic issues arising from investigations
  • Engaging effectively with a broad range of internal and external stakeholders
  • Attending sites as required to undertake investigations

About You
You will be an experienced workplace/conduct investigator with demonstrated capability personally managing investigations end-to-end.

To be successful, you will bring:

  • Demonstrated experience conducting employee conduct and/or misconduct investigations
  • Strong end-to-end investigation capability, including scoping, interviews, evidence assessment, findings and reporting
  • Experience independently managing a caseload of concurrent and potentially complex matters
  • Strong knowledge of procedural fairness and contemporary investigation practices
  • Excellent analytical, critical thinking and report-writing capability
  • Confidence handling sensitive and confidential matters
  • Strong stakeholder engagement, consultation and conflict-resolution skills
  • The ability to work autonomously and deliver within required timeframes
  • Recent Government/public-sector Conduct Investigations experience will be highly regarded

Candidates whose investigation experience is primarily in insurance, claims or other non-workplace investigative environments will not be suited to this opportunity.

The Benefits

  • $88 per hour + Super
  • Initial 6-month contract with potential extension
  • Brisbane-based Government opportunity
  • Commencing 31 August 2026
  • Hybrid flexibility following initial onboarding and training
  • Generally up to 2 days WFH once established
  • Opportunity to undertake meaningful, complex conduct investigation work within a large public-sector environment

job.title: AI Consultant
job.description:
AI Consultant – Generative AI & Adoption

Job Summary

Help organisations move from AI experimentation to practical adoption.

Translate Generative and Agentic AI solutions into tools people understand and use.

Build trusted client relationships while identifying where AI can create further value.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own day-to-day client relationships, understanding business priorities, workflows and challenges while becoming a trusted advisor on practical AI adoption.
  • Partner closely with AI Engineers to understand newly developed AI agents and Generative AI solutions, including how they work, where they add value and their limitations.
  • Translate concepts including LLMs, AI agents, copilots, RAG and workflow automation into clear, relevant language for business users.
  • Deliver practical AI training and enablement across multiple client cohorts, adapting sessions for different functions, use cases and levels of AI maturity.
  • Facilitate workshops and demonstrations that help users understand when and how to use AI solutions effectively, while capturing feedback for engineering teams.
  • Identify emerging AI opportunities through client conversations and training, helping shape potential pilots, solutions and broader consulting engagements.

What Are We Looking For

  • Strong client-facing consulting and stakeholder management experience, with the confidence to operate independently across different functions and levels of seniority.
  • Practical knowledge of Generative AI, with exposure to areas such as AI agents, LLMs, copilots, RAG or AI-enabled workflows.
  • The ability to understand technical solutions without needing to build them, then explain complex concepts clearly to non-technical audiences.
  • Strong facilitation, training and problem-solving capability, combined with commercial awareness and the ability to recognise valuable AI opportunities.

You could come from consulting, technology, digital transformation, product, business analysis, change or enablement. What matters most is your ability to operate comfortably between business and technology, learn quickly and turn complex AI solutions into practical outcomes.

If you enjoy getting under the hood of emerging AI technology and helping clients put it to work, we’d like to hear from you.

job.title: Manager Workplace Health, Safety & Wellbeing - SuniTAFE
job.description:
• Lead workplace health, safety and wellbeing systems across the organisation
  • Influence leaders to build a proactive, prevention-focused safety culture
  • Drive safety outcomes across diverse, high-risk learning environments

Lead and enhance workplace safety at SuniTAFE, partnering across diverse learning environments to build a proactive safety culture.

About the Organisation

SuniTAFE (Sunraysia Institute of TAFE) is an award-winning provider of vocational education and training across north-west Victoria. With campuses in Mildura and Swan Hill, SuniTAFE plays an important role in supporting the region’s workforce, industries and communities through practical, employment-focused education and training.

Its diverse learning environments encompass Automotive & Engineering and Construction & Trades through to Food & Hospitality, Health & Community Service and Business & Management. With approximately 5,000 students engaging with SuniTAFE each year, the organisation is committed to providing a safe and inclusive environment for employees, students and visitors.

About the Role

Reporting to the Head of People and Culture, the Manager Workplace Health, Safety & Wellbeing will lead the continued development of SuniTAFE’s safety culture, systems and risk management practices. This is a hands-on leadership role requiring someone who can combine sound technical and regulatory knowledge with a practical, consultative approach - working alongside managers to understand their environments and develop controls and processes that genuinely work.

Key priorities will include:

  • Reviewing and strengthening SuniTAFE’s health and safety management system, policies, risk framework and supporting processes.
  • Leading hazard identification, risk assessments, workplace inspections, incident investigations and the effective management of corrective actions.
  • Partnering with managers across varied teaching and operational environments to strengthen induction, safe work practices and ownership of safety.
  • Providing leadership across emergency management, safety consultation, psychosocial risk and broader employee wellbeing initiatives.

About You

You will be an experienced health and safety professional who is comfortable working across both strategic and operational priorities. You bring sound judgement and the ability to identify material risks and compliance requirements, while recognising that sustainable safety outcomes are achieved through trust, collaboration and time spent understanding how people actually work.

You will bring:

  • Relevant qualifications in occupational health and safety, workplace health and safety or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of experience and training.
  • Experience developing, implementing and improving health and safety systems within a complex or operationally diverse organisation.
  • Strong capability in risk assessment, incident management, policy development, auditing and regulatory compliance.
  • A consultative style, with the ability to coach managers and translate technical requirements into clear, practical actions.
  • Strong communication skills, together with the confidence to influence senior leaders, committees and frontline stakeholders.

This is an opportunity to make a genuine organisational impact by leading workplace health, safety and wellbeing across an organisation with a diverse operational footprint and a strong commitment to its employees, students and community. Based in Mildura you'll have the opportunity to influence executive leaders, strengthen organisational capability and build a proactive, prevention-focused safety culture that supports learning and work across the region.
